# Tree Modeler – how it works and where the numbers come from

This is a tool, not a game: the "mechanics" are the generator rules and default values.
Sources: the original's node templates (gzip XML in `templates\combined\*.stt`), the Blank
tree template (`tree_templates\Games\Blank.spm`), the original's style sheet
(`app_data\style.css`) and its code (function 0x1403175a0 lists the generation modes).
Anything marked *estimated* was looked for and not found, and was chosen by eye.

## Window layout (from a picture of the original running, checks/original/start.png)
- Menu bar: File, Edit, View, Window, Help.
- Properties panel on the left: header with the selection's name and the Generator / Node / Freehand
  mode buttons (only Generator works in this version), then collapsible groups of properties.
- Viewport in the middle (perspective by default; Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom views are orthographic).
- Dock on the right with tabs Generation (node graph), Materials, Meshes, and a toolbar
  (Add, Actions, Randomize). The original also has a Displacements tab: not in this version.
- Colours: #292929 background, #3b3b3b panels, #474747/#4f4f4f buttons, #5875b9 accent, #da9747 highlight (style.css).
- Font: Inter (the original's own font, app_data\fonts).

## Generators (nodes)
| Node | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | Shape radius 10 | Blank.spm `Shape:Radius` |
| Trunk | Mode Absolute, number 1 | Trunk.stt `Generation:Mode=3`, `Absolute:Number=1` |
| Trunk | Length 25, start angle 0.5 (straight up), radius 1 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Length:Absolute`, `Spine:Orientation:Start angle`, `Skin:Radius:Absolute` |
| Trunk | Noise amount 0.35, turbulence 0.5 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Trunk | Tip radius 0.18, base flare 0.5, 14 × 10 segments | estimated |
| Branch | First 0.215, last 0.925 | Branch.stt `Generation:First/Last` |
| Branch | Length 40 % of parent (variance 0.13 → 0.33 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Length:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Start angle 0.35 (variance 0.038 → 0.11 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Orientation:Start angle` |
| Branch | Radius 66 % of parent (variance 0.05 → 0.08 relative) | Branch.stt `Skin:Radius:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Noise 0.7, turbulence 0.5 | Branch.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Branch | Frequency 14, gravity 0.12, shorter-toward-end 0.55, tip radius 0.12 | estimated |
| Leaf | Size 1 in the template; 1.4 here, first 0 → 0.1, last 1 | Leaf.stt `Leaves:Size`, `Generation:First/Last` (size/first adjusted, estimated) |
| Leaf | Frequency 26, face sky 0.45, droop 0.15, fold 0.15, curl 0.1 | estimated |

Generation modes in the original (0x1403175a0): Classic, Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute,
Absolute steps, Phyllotaxy, Interval, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent. This version has Classic
(count per parent), Absolute (exact count), Interval (spacing along the parent) and Phyllotaxy
(nodes with N children each).

## Rules (own implementation)
- Children are spread between First and Last along each parent, each turned by the spiral
  step (137.5° default, the golden angle) plus random roll variance; Jumble shifts them along the parent.
- Start angle 0..1 maps to 0..180° from the parent's direction (0.5 = at right angles). For trunks it is
  measured up from the ground, so 0.5 is vertical.
- Length = absolute + % of parent length, times (1 − shorter-toward-end × position), times variance.
- Radius = absolute + % of parent radius at the spot, clamped to the parent; tapers to "tip radius"
  and swells by "base flare" near the base.
- Gravity bends the spine down (negative bends up); noise adds smooth wobble; jink adds sudden kinks.
- Leaves use the chosen mesh outline (Meshes tab) and material; fold bends the two halves along the
  midrib, curl bends along the length, face sky turns leaves toward the sky.

## Materials (channels from the original's .spm files)
Color, Opacity, Normal, Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface color/amount, AO, Variation (3 colours,
defaults 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.20 from Broadleaf.spm), Two sided, Cutout mesh.
Height, Custom and Custom2 channels are not in this version. Default alpha cutoff 0.33 (estimated).

## Meshes
A mesh is a cutout outline over its reference material's picture, with an anchor (attachment point)
and LODs. "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number
of points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

## Controls
- Viewport: left-drag orbit, middle-drag or Shift+left-drag pan, right-drag or wheel zoom, F frame.
- Keys: 0 perspective, 1 front (Ctrl: back), 3 right (Ctrl: left), 7 top (Ctrl: bottom), 5 toggle orthographic,
  Delete removes the selected node, Ctrl+D duplicates, Esc deselects.
- Graph: click selects, drag moves, Shift+drag onto another node re-links, right-click for a menu,
  wheel zooms, drag empty space pans. All estimated (the original's exact bindings weren't readable).

# Tree Modeler

A procedural tree modeler for games: build trees from Trunk, Branch and Leaf generator nodes,
edit materials and leaf cutout meshes, and look at the result in a perspective or orthographic viewport.

- Build: `cargo build` (Rust + macroquad).
- Run: `target/debug/tree_modeler`.
- `--screenshot <file.png>`: draws about 120 frames, saves a picture and exits.
- `--self-test <file.json>`: drives the app with scripted mouse input (orbit, select a node, drag a
  property, add a node, switch tabs) and writes the results.

See MECHANICS.md for the rules and where every default value comes from, and CREDITS.md for the
original files used.

# Tree Modeler – how it works and where the numbers come from

This is a tool, not a game: the "mechanics" are the generator rules and default values.
Sources: the original's node templates (gzip XML in `templates\combined\*.stt`), the Blank
tree template (`tree_templates\Games\Blank.spm`), the original's style sheet
(`app_data\style.css`) and its code (function 0x1403175a0 lists the generation modes).
Anything marked *estimated* was looked for and not found, and was chosen by eye.

## Window layout (from a picture of the original running, checks/original/start.png)
- Menu bar: File, Edit, View, Window, Help.
- Properties panel on the left: header with the selection's name and the Generator / Node / Freehand
  mode buttons (only Generator works in this version), then collapsible groups of properties.
- Viewport in the middle (perspective by default; Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom views are orthographic).
- Dock on the right with tabs Generation (node graph), Materials, Meshes, and a toolbar
  (Add, Actions, Randomize). The original also has a Displacements tab: not in this version.
- Colours: #292929 background, #3b3b3b panels, #474747/#4f4f4f buttons, #5875b9 accent, #da9747 highlight (style.css).
- Font: Inter (the original's own font, app_data\fonts).

## Generators (nodes)
| Node | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | Shape radius 10 | Blank.spm `Shape:Radius` |
| Trunk | Mode Absolute, number 1 | Trunk.stt `Generation:Mode=3`, `Absolute:Number=1` |
| Trunk | Length 25, start angle 0.5 (straight up), radius 1 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Length:Absolute`, `Spine:Orientation:Start angle`, `Skin:Radius:Absolute` |
| Trunk | Noise amount 0.35, turbulence 0.5 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Trunk | Tip radius 0.18, base flare 0.5, 14 × 10 segments | estimated |
| Branch | First 0.215, last 0.925 | Branch.stt `Generation:First/Last` |
| Branch | Length 40 % of parent (variance 0.13 → 0.33 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Length:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Start angle 0.35 (variance 0.038 → 0.11 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Orientation:Start angle` |
| Branch | Radius 66 % of parent (variance 0.05 → 0.08 relative) | Branch.stt `Skin:Radius:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Noise 0.7, turbulence 0.5 | Branch.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Branch | Frequency 14, gravity 0.12, shorter-toward-end 0.55, tip radius 0.12 | estimated |
| Leaf | Size 1 in the template; 1.4 here, first 0 → 0.1, last 1 | Leaf.stt `Leaves:Size`, `Generation:First/Last` (size/first adjusted, estimated) |
| Leaf | Frequency 26, face sky 0.45, droop 0.15, fold 0.15, curl 0.1 | estimated |

Generation modes in the original (0x1403175a0): Classic, Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute,
Absolute steps, Phyllotaxy, Interval, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent. This version has Classic
(count per parent), Absolute (exact count), Interval (spacing along the parent) and Phyllotaxy
(nodes with N children each).

## Rules (own implementation)
- Children are spread between First and Last along each parent, each turned by the spiral
  step (137.5° default, the golden angle) plus random roll variance; Jumble shifts them along the parent.
- Start angle 0..1 maps to 0..180° from the parent's direction (0.5 = at right angles). For trunks it is
  measured up from the ground, so 0.5 is vertical.
- Length = absolute + % of parent length, times (1 − shorter-toward-end × position), times variance.
- Radius = absolute + % of parent radius at the spot, clamped to the parent; tapers to "tip radius"
  and swells by "base flare" near the base.
- Gravity bends the spine down (negative bends up); noise adds smooth wobble; jink adds sudden kinks.
- Leaves use the chosen mesh outline (Meshes tab) and material; fold bends the two halves along the
  midrib, curl bends along the length, face sky turns leaves toward the sky.

## Materials (channels from the original's .spm files)
Color, Opacity, Normal, Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface color/amount, AO, Variation (3 colours,
defaults 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.20 from Broadleaf.spm), Two sided, Cutout mesh.
Height, Custom and Custom2 channels are not in this version. Default alpha cutoff 0.33 (estimated).

## Meshes
A mesh is a cutout outline over its reference material's picture, with an anchor (attachment point)
and LODs. "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number
of points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

## Controls
- Viewport: left-drag orbit, middle-drag or Shift+left-drag pan, right-drag or wheel zoom, F frame.
- Keys: 0 perspective, 1 front (Ctrl: back), 3 right (Ctrl: left), 7 top (Ctrl: bottom), 5 toggle orthographic,
  Delete removes the selected node, Ctrl+D duplicates, Esc deselects.
- Graph: click selects, drag moves, Shift+drag onto another node re-links, right-click for a menu,
  wheel zooms, drag empty space pans. All estimated (the original's exact bindings weren't readable).

content.text:
I finished the first version of your tree modeler, and Craft Anything's check passes: it builds, starts, and its self-test can orbit the camera, select a node, change a setting, add a node and open both editors.

- **Node graph:** add Trunk, Branch and Leaf nodes (they use the original's node icons) and they grow a 3D tree right away.
- **Properties panel:** on the left, filled in for whatever node, material or mesh you click. The starting settings come from the original's own node templates.
- **Material editor:** procedural bark and leaf textures, or load your own image. It has colour, opacity, bump, gloss and subsurface controls, plus a live preview.
- **Mesh editor:** you draw leaf cutout shapes over the texture, and it can generate one automatically and make simpler versions for distant detail levels.
- **Viewport:** perspective by default, with Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views that switch to orthographic.

Not in this version yet:
- The original's Displacements tab.
- Its "Node" and "Freehand" editing modes (the buttons are there but greyed out).
- Six of its ten ways to place branches: I built Classic, Absolute, Interval and Phyllotaxy.
- Saving or exporting trees.

Two things are my best guess rather than copied from the original. I couldn't see inside its material and mesh editors without a tree loaded, so those layouts are mine. Some starting numbers, like how many branches and leaves appear, I chose by eye.

There are no tree presets. File › New tree starts you with just the Tree node, but the app opens with one default Trunk, Branch and Leaf so there's something on screen.

A good next request: send me a picture of the original's Material or Mesh editor so I can match it, or ask for the curve editors the original uses to shape a property along a branch.

input.old_string:
## Rules (own implementation)
- Children are spread between First and Last along each parent, each turned by the spiral
  step (137.5° default, the golden angle) plus random roll variance; Jumble shifts them along the parent.
input.new_string:
## Placement rules read from the original's code (Ghidra pseudo-code)
Constants were read directly: 1.0 at 0x141f409b4, 0.5 at 0x141f407a8, 0.025 at 0x141f4040c,
10.0 at 0x141f40d74, 0.1 at 0x141f404b4, 0.25 at 0x141f405e0. Roll is measured in turns (1.0 = 360°).
Random numbers come from a 10000-entry table indexed by seeds that wrap at 9999 (0x141eb5fa0);
this build uses its own random generator instead (same kind of result, different exact trees).

- **Classic** (fn 0x140477e40, properties wired in fn 0x1404766f0):
  - count = whole part of Frequency (Style Absolute), or parent length × Frequency × 0.025
    (Style Relative). Fractions are dropped, not rounded.
  - each child sits at a random spot between First and Last, drawn from the frequency curve
    (fn 0x1402cad40; a flat curve gives evenly random spots).
  - roll (turns) = (Balanced ? i / n : random 0..1) + random(−Offset, +Offset) × 0.5, all × Sweep,
    then + Roll. With "Centered align" the rolls are shifted by −(max+min)/2.
- **Absolute** (fn 0x1404723f0): count = Number; roll = (i / n + random(−Jumble, +Jumble) × 0.5) × Sweep,
  centred on zero, then + Roll; positions random between First and Last.
- **Interval** (fn 0x14047b6f0): start at Last and step down to First by (10 / Frequency) length
  units; each node gets Count children 1/Count turn apart (½ turn when Count < 3), every node adds
  Spiral × 0.1 turns, Spread jitters children along the parent, Limit caps the node count.
- Switching to Interval converts Frequency: new = max(0, (int)(old + 0.5) − 1) or old × 0.9 (fn 0x1404799a0).
- Phyllotaxy here reuses the Interval walk with "Internode length" in units (the original's
  phyllotaxy routine wasn't read; estimated).

## Property limits read from the original's property tables
Spine table fn 0x14053b8c0, skin table fn 0x140540c10 (each entry: type, suggested slider top,
hard min, hard max). Property numbers: Length:Absolute = 3, Start angle = 4, Gravity = 130, Jink:Amount = 180.
| Property | Range in original | Suggested slider top |
|---|---|---|
| Spine:Length:Absolute | 0 … ∞ | 20 |
| Spine:Length:+ % of parent | 0 … ∞ | 0.5 |
| Spine:Orientation:Start angle | 0 … 1 | — |
| Spine:Orientation:Roll, Spine:Shape:Ancestor | −1 … 1 | — |

# Tree Modeler – how it works and where the numbers come from

This is a tool, not a game: the "mechanics" are the generator rules and default values.
Sources: the original's node templates (gzip XML in `templates\combined\*.stt`), the Blank
tree template (`tree_templates\Games\Blank.spm`), the original's style sheet
(`app_data\style.css`) and its code (function 0x1403175a0 lists the generation modes).
Anything marked *estimated* was looked for and not found, and was chosen by eye.

## Window layout (from a picture of the original running, checks/original/start.png)
- Menu bar: File, Edit, View, Window, Help.
- Properties panel on the left: header with the selection's name and the Generator / Node / Freehand
  mode buttons (only Generator works in this version), then collapsible groups of properties.
- Viewport in the middle (perspective by default; Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom views are orthographic).
- Dock on the right with tabs Generation (node graph), Materials, Meshes, and a toolbar
  (Add, Actions, Randomize). The original also has a Displacements tab: not in this version.
- Colours: #292929 background, #3b3b3b panels, #474747/#4f4f4f buttons, #5875b9 accent, #da9747 highlight (style.css).
- Font: Inter (the original's own font, app_data\fonts).

## Generators (nodes)
| Node | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | Shape radius 10 | Blank.spm `Shape:Radius` |
| Trunk | Mode Absolute, number 1 | Trunk.stt `Generation:Mode=3`, `Absolute:Number=1` |
| Trunk | Length 25, start angle 0.5 (straight up), radius 1 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Length:Absolute`, `Spine:Orientation:Start angle`, `Skin:Radius:Absolute` |
| Trunk | Noise amount 0.35, turbulence 0.5 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Trunk | Tip radius 0.18, base flare 0.5, 14 × 10 segments | estimated |
| Branch | First 0.215, last 0.925 | Branch.stt `Generation:First/Last` |
| Branch | Length 40 % of parent (variance 0.13 → 0.33 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Length:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Start angle 0.35 (variance 0.038 → 0.11 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Orientation:Start angle` |
| Branch | Radius 66 % of parent (variance 0.05 → 0.08 relative) | Branch.stt `Skin:Radius:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Noise 0.7, turbulence 0.5 | Branch.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Branch | Frequency 14, gravity 0.12, shorter-toward-end 0.55, tip radius 0.12 | estimated |
| Leaf | Size 1 in the template; 1.4 here, first 0 → 0.1, last 1 | Leaf.stt `Leaves:Size`, `Generation:First/Last` (size/first adjusted, estimated) |
| Leaf | Frequency 26, face sky 0.45, droop 0.15, fold 0.15, curl 0.1 | estimated |

Generation modes in the original (0x1403175a0): Classic, Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute,
Absolute steps, Phyllotaxy, Interval, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent. This version has Classic
(count per parent), Absolute (exact count), Interval (spacing along the parent) and Phyllotaxy
(nodes with N children each).

## Rules (own implementation)
- Children are spread between First and Last along each parent, each turned by the spiral
  step (137.5° default, the golden angle) plus random roll variance; Jumble shifts them along the parent.
- Start angle 0..1 maps to 0..180° from the parent's direction (0.5 = at right angles). For trunks it is
  measured up from the ground, so 0.5 is vertical.
- Length = absolute + % of parent length, times (1 − shorter-toward-end × position), times variance.
- Radius = absolute + % of parent radius at the spot, clamped to the parent; tapers to "tip radius"
  and swells by "base flare" near the base.
- Gravity bends the spine down (negative bends up); noise adds smooth wobble; jink adds sudden kinks.
- Leaves use the chosen mesh outline (Meshes tab) and material; fold bends the two halves along the
  midrib, curl bends along the length, face sky turns leaves toward the sky.

## Materials (channels from the original's .spm files)
Color, Opacity, Normal, Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface color/amount, AO, Variation (3 colours,
defaults 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.20 from Broadleaf.spm), Two sided, Cutout mesh.
Height, Custom and Custom2 channels are not in this version. Default alpha cutoff 0.33 (estimated).

## Meshes
A mesh is a cutout outline over its reference material's picture, with an anchor (attachment point)
and LODs. "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number
of points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

## Controls
- Viewport: left-drag orbit, middle-drag or Shift+left-drag pan, right-drag or wheel zoom, F frame.
- Keys: 0 perspective, 1 front (Ctrl: back), 3 right (Ctrl: left), 7 top (Ctrl: bottom), 5 toggle orthographic,
  Delete removes the selected node, Ctrl+D duplicates, Esc deselects.
- Graph: click selects, drag moves, Shift+drag onto another node re-links, right-click for a menu,
  wheel zooms, drag empty space pans. All estimated (the original's exact bindings weren't readable).

## Rules (own implementation)
- Children are spread between First and Last along each parent, each turned by the spiral

input.new_string:
## Placement rules read from the original's code (Ghidra pseudo-code)
Constants were read directly: 1.0 at 0x141f409b4, 0.5 at 0x141f407a8, 0.025 at 0x141f4040c,
10.0 at 0x141f40d74, 0.1 at 0x141f404b4, 0.25 at 0x141f405e0. Roll is measured in turns (1.0 = 360°).
Random numbers come from a 10000-entry table indexed by seeds that wrap at 9999 (0x141eb5fa0);
this build uses its own random generator instead (same kind of result, different exact trees).

- **Classic** (fn 0x140477e40, properties wired in fn 0x1404766f0):
  - count = whole part of Frequency (Style Absolute), or parent length × Frequency × 0.025
    (Style Relative). Fractions are dropped, not rounded.
  - each child sits at a random spot between First and Last, drawn from the frequency curve
    (fn 0x1402cad40; a flat curve gives evenly random spots).
  - roll (turns) = (Balanced ? i / n : random 0..1) + random(−Offset, +Offset) × 0.5, all × Sweep,
    then + Roll. With "Centered align" the rolls are shifted by −(max+min)/2.
- **Absolute** (fn 0x1404723f0): count = Number; roll = (i / n + random(−Jumble, +Jumble) × 0.5) × Sweep,
  centred on zero, then + Roll; positions random between First and Last.
- **Interval** (fn 0x14047b6f0): start at Last and step down to First by (10 / Frequency) length
  units; each node gets Count children 1/Count turn apart (½ turn when Count < 3), every node adds
  Spiral × 0.1 turns, Spread jitters children along the parent, Limit caps the node count.
- Switching to Interval converts Frequency: new = max(0, (int)(old + 0.5) − 1) or old × 0.9 (fn 0x1404799a0).
- Phyllotaxy here reuses the Interval walk with "Internode length" in units (the original's
  phyllotaxy routine wasn't read; estimated).

## Property limits read from the original's property tables
Spine table fn 0x14053b8c0, skin table fn 0x140540c10 (each entry: type, suggested slider top,
hard min, hard max). Property numbers: Length:Absolute = 3, Start angle = 4, Gravity = 130, Jink:Amount = 180.
| Property | Range in original | Suggested slider top |
|---|---|---|
| Spine:Length:Absolute | 0 … ∞ | 20 |
| Spine:Length:+ % of parent | 0 … ∞ | 0.5 |
| Spine:Orientation:Start angle | 0 … 1 | — |
| Spine:Orientation:Roll, Spine:Shape:Ancestor | −1 … 1 | — |
| Spine:Shape:Gravity, Spine:Shape:Twist | unbounded | — |
| Spine:Shape:Straightness, Spine:Jink:Amount, Jink:Uniformity | 0 … 1 | uniformity 0.1 |
| Spine:Jink:+ Relative | 0 … ∞ | 0.1 |
| Segments:Radial:Absolute | 0 … 100000 (whole) | 3 |
| Skin:Radius:+ % of parent | 0 … ∞ | 0.75 |
| Skin:Radius:Length compensation | 0 … ∞ | 1 |
| Skin:Radius:Length kill ratio | 0 … ∞ | 500 |
| Skin:Roll | −1 … 1 | — |
| Skin:Smooth, Skin:Squash:Amount | 0 … 1 | — |

## Rules this build adds itself (not found in the code yet; estimated)
- The spine walk (how gravity, noise and jink bend a branch) and the radius taper: the routine that
  applies them wasn't located (it reads properties through cached pointers, not by name). Gravity
  bends the spine down by gravity × 2.5 / segments per step; noise is a smooth wobble; both estimated.

content.text:
I decompiled the original's branch placement code and rebuilt the app to follow it. The build passes Craft Anything's check, including the self-test.

**What the original actually does, and what changed:**
- **Classic mode:** the number of branches is Frequency with any fraction dropped. Each branch lands at a random height between First and Last; before, I spaced them evenly with a little jitter. How far each one turns around the parent is controlled by the original's own settings, so the panel now has Balanced, Offset, Sweep and Roll in place of my "spiral step" and "roll variance". There is also a new Relative style, where the count is parent length × Frequency × 0.025.
- **Absolute mode:** branches are spread evenly around the parent with a bit of random wobble, then centred.
- **Interval mode:** it walks down the parent from Last in steps of 10 ÷ Frequency, putting a set number of branches at each step. Its Spiral setting adds a little extra turn at each step.
- **Slider limits:** several now come from the original's own property tables. For example, start angle runs 0 to 1, Roll runs −1 to 1, and jink runs 0 to 1.

These rules and their code locations are written into the values sheet, which now lists 37 values traced to the original and 15 still estimated.

**Still estimated:**
- **How a branch bends** (gravity, wobble, sudden kinks) and **how it thins toward the tip.** I couldn't find the code that applies them, because it doesn't refer to those settings by name. Those rules are still my own approximation.
- **Exact tree shapes.** The original draws its random numbers from a built-in table; I use my own generator, so the same seed won't give an identical tree.
- **Phyllotaxy mode** reuses the Interval walk, because I didn't decompile the original's version.
- **Inside the material and mesh editors.** I couldn't see them in the running original, so those layouts are still my design.

A good next step would be to ask me to keep tracing the branch-bending code, which would make the shapes closer to the original's.

# Handoff – Tree Modeler (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

## Where things stand
- **Builds and passes all checks** (build, screenshot, self-test, mechanics sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad, code in `src/`:
  - `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs (Generation graph, Materials, Meshes), viewport
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel (left)
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `render.rs`: lit shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: procedural textures and auto-cutout
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Done:**
  - Node graph with Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes (the original's own icons): add, link, duplicate, hide, delete, randomize.
  - Properties panel grouped like the original (Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation).
  - Material editor: procedural bark and leaf, image loading, colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours, live sphere/card preview.
  - Mesh editor: leaf cutout points over the texture, anchor point, auto-generate from alpha, LODs.
  - Viewport: perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); grid; frame; lighting settings.
- **Decompiled from the original** (details in `MECHANICS.md`):
  - Classic placement: fn 0x140477e40.
  - Absolute placement: fn 0x1404723f0.
  - Interval placement: fn 0x14047b6f0.
  - Position sampling: fn 0x1402cad40.
  - Property limit tables: fn 0x14053b8c0 (spine) and fn 0x140540c10 (skin).
  - Generation mode list: fn 0x1403175a0.
  - Property ids = (table offset − 0x48) / 0xC8 (Start angle 4, Gravity 130, Jink 180).
  - Class method tables (found via RTTI): CGenAlgClassic 0x141f181a0, CBranchNode 0x141f26988, CSpineNode 0x141f37d38.

## Still estimated / open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers. The code that applies them reads cached property pointers, not names, so it wasn't found.
2. Phyllotaxy mode reuses the Interval walk; the original's phyllotaxy routine wasn't read.
3. The layout inside the Material and Mesh editors is my design; the original's couldn't be seen without a tree loaded.
4. The original draws randomness from a built-in table, so the same seed won't give an identical tree.
5. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab.
   - Node and Freehand edit modes (buttons shown greyed out).
   - The other six generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent.
   - Property curves (splines).
   - Saving, loading and exporting trees.
   - Wind and LOD export.

## Next steps (in order)
1. **Trace the spine walk.** Follow callers of fn 0x1403154a0 (the per-child evaluator) from the placement routines, or walk the CBranchNode method table in Ghidra, to find where Gravity (property 130) is applied. Replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs` (`make_spine`, `build_spine`).
2. **Add property curves.** Give Frequency, Length and Radius a small curve editor in the Properties panel; the original evaluates these as splines along the parent.
3. **Save and load trees** (a simple JSON file), then add OBJ/FBX export for game engines.
4. **Add the remaining generation modes**, starting with Proportional and Bifurcation (their property names are already known from the templates).
5. **Ask the person for pictures** of the original's Material and Mesh editors, and match their layout.
6. **Add Node and Freehand edit modes** (select and adjust individual branches in the viewport).

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots.
- Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units. The UI scale lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Node templates in `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Modeler v10.2.0\templates\combined\*.stt` are gzip XML holding real defaults.

## Meshes (Meshes tab, matching the original's Meshes panel)
Read from the 8.4.2 program: panel layout, labels, tooltips and choices in fn 0x140076fd0,
Orient choices and their stored values plus Copy/Paste/Duplicate in fn 0x140084750. Fields match the
original's <Mesh> data in .spm files (FixWinding, FlipNormals, CollisionScale, Weight, Wind, Flip,
Orient, SpineStyle, PivotStyle, Collection, MoreLodsMeshID, Scale, Lod_1/Lod_2).
- Top row: drag handle (drop on the viewport: the selected Leaf generator, or the first one, uses
  the mesh), mesh picker, +/- (add card / add cutout from the reference material / remove),
  + (load an OBJ file as a new mesh), Copy / Paste / Duplicate.
- Geometry: Edit Mesh... opens the cutout editor (points and anchor over the picture). High / Med /
  Low are three levels; each is a cutout or a loaded OBJ file, with Browse..., Reload and Export (OBJ).
  An empty level uses the level above. More: another mesh supplies levels 3 and lower.
- Show: which level the preview and the cutout editor use. Alignment: draws the intended
  orientation (a leaf in X/Y growing up +Y from the origin, facing +Z). V:F = vertices and faces.
- Transform: Orient (Z-Up Right-handed = 6 default, Y-Up Right-handed 7, Z-Up Left-handed 8,
  Y-Up Left-handed 9, XYZ 0, XZY 1, YXZ 2, YZX 3, ZXY 4, ZYX 5), Flip (X Y Z … -X -Y -Z),
  Flip normals, Fix winding. The axis maths of each Orient choice is this build's reading of the
  labels (estimated). A mirroring choice reverses the faces.
- Collection: when on, the mesh is built when the tree computes from every Trunk/Branch generator
  marked "Contribute to collections" (Spines: Branches / Fronds / Both — this build has no fronds;
  Pivot: Origin keeps world positions, First makes them relative to the first collected spine).
- Wind direction: Growth (+X +Y +Z -X -Y -Z) is the mesh axis that points along the leaf when placed
  (default +Y, from the sample's WindY = 1); Ripple (Normal, X, Y, Z) is stored for the wind system
  (this build has no wind yet).
- Proxy collision: Scale and Weight are stored (used for world-building proxies in the original;
  not used by anything in this build yet).
- "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number of
  points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# TreeCraft – how it works and where the numbers come from

This is a tool, not a game: the "mechanics" are the generator rules and default values.
Sources: the original's node templates (gzip XML in `templates\combined\*.stt`), the Blank
tree template (`tree_templates\Games\Blank.spm`), the original's style sheet
(`app_data\style.css`) and its code (function 0x1403175a0 lists the generation modes).
Anything marked *estimated* was looked for and not found, and was chosen by eye.

## Window layout (from a picture of the original running, checks/original/start.png)
- Menu bar: File, Edit, View, Window, Help.
- Properties panel on the left: header with the selection's name and the Generator / Node / Freehand
  mode buttons (only Generator works in this version), then collapsible groups of properties.
- Viewport in the middle (perspective by default; Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom views are orthographic).
- Dock on the right with tabs Generation (node graph), Materials, Meshes, and a toolbar
  (Add, Actions, Randomize). The original also has a Displacements tab: not in this version.
- Colours: #292929 background, #3b3b3b panels, #474747/#4f4f4f buttons, #5875b9 accent, #da9747 highlight (style.css).
- Font: Inter (the original's own font, app_data\fonts).

## Generators (nodes)
| Node | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | Shape radius 10 | Blank.spm `Shape:Radius` |
| Trunk | Mode Absolute, number 1 | Trunk.stt `Generation:Mode=3`, `Absolute:Number=1` |
| Trunk | Length 25, start angle 0.5 (straight up), radius 1 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Length:Absolute`, `Spine:Orientation:Start angle`, `Skin:Radius:Absolute` |
| Trunk | Noise amount 0.35, turbulence 0.5 | Trunk.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Trunk | Tip radius 0.18, base flare 0.5, 14 × 10 segments | estimated |
| Branch | First 0.215, last 0.925 | Branch.stt `Generation:First/Last` |
| Branch | Length 40 % of parent (variance 0.13 → 0.33 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Length:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Start angle 0.35 (variance 0.038 → 0.11 relative) | Branch.stt `Spine:Orientation:Start angle` |
| Branch | Radius 66 % of parent (variance 0.05 → 0.08 relative) | Branch.stt `Skin:Radius:+ % of parent` |
| Branch | Noise 0.7, turbulence 0.5 | Branch.stt `Spine:Noise:Late:*` |
| Branch | Interval count 4, spread 0.5; Balanced on, Offset 0, Sweep 1, Roll 0 | Branch.stt `Generation:Interval:*`, `Generation:Orientation:*` |
| Branch | Frequency 14, gravity 0.12, shorter-toward-end 0.55, tip radius 0.12 | estimated |
| Leaf | Size 1 in the template; 1.4 here, first 0 → 0.1, last 1 | Leaf.stt `Leaves:Size`, `Generation:First/Last` (size/first adjusted, estimated) |
| Leaf | Frequency 26, face sky 0.45, droop 0.15, fold 0.15, curl 0.1 | estimated |

Generation modes in the original (0x1403175a0): Classic, Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute,
Absolute steps, Phyllotaxy, Interval, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent. This version has Classic
(count per parent), Absolute (exact count), Interval (spacing along the parent) and Phyllotaxy
(nodes with N children each).

## Placement rules read from the original's code (Ghidra pseudo-code)
Constants were read directly: 1.0 at 0x141f409b4, 0.5 at 0x141f407a8, 0.025 at 0x141f4040c,
10.0 at 0x141f40d74, 0.1 at 0x141f404b4, 0.25 at 0x141f405e0. Roll is measured in turns (1.0 = 360°).
Random numbers come from a 10000-entry table indexed by seeds that wrap at 9999 (0x141eb5fa0);
this build uses its own random generator instead (same kind of result, different exact trees).

- **Classic** (fn 0x140477e40, properties wired in fn 0x1404766f0):
  - count = whole part of Frequency (Style Absolute), or parent length × Frequency × 0.025
    (Style Relative). Fractions are dropped, not rounded.
  - each child sits at a random spot between First and Last, drawn from the frequency curve
    (fn 0x1402cad40; a flat curve gives evenly random spots).
  - roll (turns) = (Balanced ? i / n : random 0..1) + random(−Offset, +Offset) × 0.5, all × Sweep,
    then + Roll. With "Centered align" the rolls are shifted by −(max+min)/2.
- **Absolute** (fn 0x1404723f0): count = Number; roll = (i / n + random(−Jumble, +Jumble) × 0.5) × Sweep,
  centred on zero, then + Roll; positions random between First and Last.
- **Interval** (fn 0x14047b6f0): start at Last and step down to First by (10 / Frequency) length
  units; each node gets Count children 1/Count turn apart (½ turn when Count < 3), every node adds
  Spiral × 0.1 turns, Spread jitters children along the parent, Limit caps the node count.
- Switching to Interval converts Frequency: new = max(0, (int)(old + 0.5) − 1) or old × 0.9 (fn 0x1404799a0).
- Phyllotaxy here reuses the Interval walk with "Internode length" in units (the original's
  phyllotaxy routine wasn't read; estimated).

## Property limits read from the original's property tables
Spine table fn 0x14053b8c0, skin table fn 0x140540c10 (each entry: type, suggested slider top,
hard min, hard max). Property numbers: Length:Absolute = 3, Start angle = 4, Gravity = 130, Jink:Amount = 180.
| Property | Range in original | Suggested slider top |
|---|---|---|
| Spine:Length:Absolute | 0 … ∞ | 20 |
| Spine:Length:+ % of parent | 0 … ∞ | 0.5 |
| Spine:Orientation:Start angle | 0 … 1 | — |
| Spine:Orientation:Roll, Spine:Shape:Ancestor | −1 … 1 | — |
| Spine:Shape:Gravity, Spine:Shape:Twist | unbounded | — |
| Spine:Shape:Straightness, Spine:Jink:Amount, Jink:Uniformity | 0 … 1 | uniformity 0.1 |
| Spine:Jink:+ Relative | 0 … ∞ | 0.1 |
| Segments:Radial:Absolute | 0 … 100000 (whole) | 3 |
| Skin:Radius:+ % of parent | 0 … ∞ | 0.75 |
| Skin:Radius:Length compensation | 0 … ∞ | 1 |
| Skin:Radius:Length kill ratio | 0 … ∞ | 500 |
| Skin:Roll | −1 … 1 | — |
| Skin:Smooth, Skin:Squash:Amount | 0 … 1 | — |

## Rules this build adds itself (not found in the code yet; estimated)
- The spine walk (how gravity, noise and jink bend a branch) and the radius taper: the routine that
  applies them wasn't located (it reads properties through cached pointers, not by name). Gravity
  bends the spine down by gravity × 2.5 / segments per step; noise is a smooth wobble; both estimated.
- Start angle 0..1 maps to 0..180° from the parent's direction (0.5 = at right angles). For trunks it is
  measured up from the ground, so 0.5 is vertical.
- Length = absolute + % of parent length, times (1 − shorter-toward-end × position), times variance.
- Radius = absolute + % of parent radius at the spot, clamped to the parent; tapers to "tip radius"
  and swells by "base flare" near the base.
- Gravity bends the spine down (negative bends up); noise adds smooth wobble; jink adds sudden kinks.
- Leaves use the chosen mesh outline (Meshes tab) and material; fold bends the two halves along the
  midrib, curl bends along the length, face sky turns leaves toward the sky.

## Materials (channels from the original's .spm files)
Color, Opacity, Normal, Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface color/amount, AO, Variation (3 colours,
defaults 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.20 from Broadleaf.spm), Two sided, Cutout mesh.
Height, Custom and Custom2 channels are not in this version. Default alpha cutoff 0.33 (estimated).

## Meshes
A mesh is a cutout outline over its reference material's picture, with an anchor (attachment point)
and LODs. "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number
of points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

## Controls
- Viewport: left-drag orbit, middle-drag or Shift+left-drag pan, right-drag or wheel zoom, F frame.
- Keys: 0 perspective, 1 front (Ctrl: back), 3 right (Ctrl: left), 7 top (Ctrl: bottom), 5 toggle orthographic,
  Delete removes the selected node, Ctrl+D duplicates, Esc deselects.
- Graph: click selects, drag moves, Shift+drag onto another node re-links, right-click for a menu,
  wheel zooms, drag empty space pans. All estimated (the original's exact bindings weren't readable).

lines: defaults 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.20 from Broadleaf.spm), Two sided, Cutout mesh.
Height, Custom and Custom2 channels are not in this version. Default alpha cutoff 0.33 (estimated).

+  Y-Up Left-handed 9, XYZ 0, XZY 1, YXZ 2, YZX 3, ZXY 4, ZYX 5), Flip (X Y Z … -X -Y -Z),
+  Flip normals, Fix winding. The axis maths of each Orient choice is this build's reading of the
+  labels (estimated). A mirroring choice reverses the faces.
+- Collection: when on, the mesh is built when the tree computes from every Trunk/Branch generator
+  marked "Contribute to collections" (Spines: Branches / Fronds / Both — this build has no fronds;
+  Pivot: Origin keeps world positions, First makes them relative to the first collected spine).
+- Wind direction: Growth (+X +Y +Z -X -Y -Z) is the mesh axis that points along the leaf when placed
+  (default +Y, from the sample's WindY = 1); Ripple (Normal, X, Y, Z) is stored for the wind system
+- Proxy collision: Scale and Weight are stored (used for world-building proxies in the original;
+  not used by anything in this build yet).
+- "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number of
+  points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).
- Viewport: left-drag orbit, middle-drag or Shift+left-drag pan, right-drag or wheel zoom, F frame.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

## Where things stand
- **Builds and passes all checks** (build, screenshot, self-test, mechanics sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad, code in `src/`:
  - `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs (Generation graph, Materials, Meshes), viewport
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel (left)
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `render.rs`: lit shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: procedural textures and auto-cutout
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Done:**
  - Node graph with Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes (the original's own icons): add, link, duplicate, hide, delete, randomize.
  - Properties panel grouped like the original (Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation).
  - Material editor: procedural bark and leaf, image loading, colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours, live sphere/card preview.
  - Mesh editor: leaf cutout points over the texture, anchor point, auto-generate from alpha, LODs.
  - Viewport: perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); grid; frame; lighting settings.
- **Decompiled from the original** (details in `MECHANICS.md`):
  - Classic placement: fn 0x140477e40.
  - Absolute placement: fn 0x1404723f0.
  - Interval placement: fn 0x14047b6f0.
  - Position sampling: fn 0x1402cad40.
  - Property limit tables: fn 0x14053b8c0 (spine) and fn 0x140540c10 (skin).
  - Generation mode list: fn 0x1403175a0.
  - Property ids = (table offset − 0x48) / 0xC8 (Start angle 4, Gravity 130, Jink 180).
  - Class method tables (found via RTTI): CGenAlgClassic 0x141f181a0, CBranchNode 0x141f26988, CSpineNode 0x141f37d38.

## Still estimated / open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers. The code that applies them reads cached property pointers, not names, so it wasn't found.
2. Phyllotaxy mode reuses the Interval walk; the original's phyllotaxy routine wasn't read.
3. The layout inside the Material and Mesh editors is my design; the original's couldn't be seen without a tree loaded.
4. The original draws randomness from a built-in table, so the same seed won't give an identical tree.
5. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab.
   - Node and Freehand edit modes (buttons shown greyed out).
   - The other six generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent.
   - Property curves (splines).
   - Saving, loading and exporting trees.
   - Wind and LOD export.

## Next steps (in order)
1. **Trace the spine walk.** Follow callers of fn 0x1403154a0 (the per-child evaluator) from the placement routines, or walk the CBranchNode method table in Ghidra, to find where Gravity (property 130) is applied. Replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs` (`make_spine`, `build_spine`).
2. **Add property curves.** Give Frequency, Length and Radius a small curve editor in the Properties panel; the original evaluates these as splines along the parent.
3. **Save and load trees** (a simple JSON file), then add OBJ/FBX export for game engines.
4. **Add the remaining generation modes**, starting with Proportional and Bifurcation (their property names are already known from the templates).
5. **Ask the person for pictures** of the original's Material and Mesh editors, and match their layout.
6. **Add Node and Freehand edit modes** (select and adjust individual branches in the viewport).

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots.
- Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units. The UI scale lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Node templates in `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Modeler v10.2.0\templates\combined\*.stt` are gzip XML holding real defaults.

- Geometry: Edit Mesh... opens the cutout editor (points and anchor over the picture). High / Med /
  Low are three levels; each is a cutout or a loaded OBJ file, with Browse..., Reload and Export (OBJ).
  An empty level uses the level above. More: another mesh supplies levels 3 and lower.
- Show: which level the preview and the cutout editor use. Alignment: draws the intended
  orientation (a leaf in X/Y growing up +Y from the origin, facing +Z). V:F = vertices and faces.
- Transform: Orient (Z-Up Right-handed = 6 default, Y-Up Right-handed 7, Z-Up Left-handed 8,
  Y-Up Left-handed 9, XYZ 0, XZY 1, YXZ 2, YZX 3, ZXY 4, ZYX 5), Flip (X Y Z … -X -Y -Z),
  Flip normals, Fix winding. The axis maths of each Orient choice is this build's reading of the
  labels (estimated). A mirroring choice reverses the faces.
- Collection: when on, the mesh is built when the tree computes from every Trunk/Branch generator
  marked "Contribute to collections" (Spines: Branches / Fronds / Both — this build has no fronds;
  Pivot: Origin keeps world positions, First makes them relative to the first collected spine).
- Wind direction: Growth (+X +Y +Z -X -Y -Z) is the mesh axis that points along the leaf when placed
  (default +Y, from the sample's WindY = 1); Ripple (Normal, X, Y, Z) is stored for the wind system
  (this build has no wind yet).
- Proxy collision: Scale and Weight are stored (used for world-building proxies in the original;
  not used by anything in this build yet).
- "Generate from material" makes an outline around the opaque pixels with the chosen number of
  points (own method: convex outline, then corners merged while keeping the leaf covered).

## Where things stand
- **Builds and passes all checks** (build, screenshot, self-test, mechanics sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad, code in `src/`:
  - `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs (Generation graph, Materials, Meshes), viewport
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel (left)
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `render.rs`: lit shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: procedural textures and auto-cutout
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Done:**
  - Node graph with Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes (the original's own icons): add, link, duplicate, hide, delete, randomize.
  - Properties panel grouped like the original (Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation).
  - Material editor: procedural bark and leaf, image loading, colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours, live sphere/card preview.
  - Mesh editor: leaf cutout points over the texture, anchor point, auto-generate from alpha, LODs.
  - Viewport: perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); grid; frame; lighting settings.
- **Decompiled from the original** (details in `MECHANICS.md`):
  - Classic placement: fn 0x140477e40.
  - Absolute placement: fn 0x1404723f0.
  - Interval placement: fn 0x14047b6f0.
  - Position sampling: fn 0x1402cad40.
  - Property limit tables: fn 0x14053b8c0 (spine) and fn 0x140540c10 (skin).
  - Generation mode list: fn 0x1403175a0.
  - Property ids = (table offset − 0x48) / 0xC8 (Start angle 4, Gravity 130, Jink 180).
  - Class method tables (found via RTTI): CGenAlgClassic 0x141f181a0, CBranchNode 0x141f26988, CSpineNode 0x141f37d38.

## Meshes tab (added 2026-11-08)
- Rebuilt to match the original's Meshes panel (read from the 8.4.2 program, fn 0x140076fd0 / 0x140084750).
  The person now has SpeedTree Games Indie 8.4.2 installed: `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe` (the 10.2 copy is gone).
- Code: `src/meshio.rs` handles OBJ load/save, cutout → geometry, Orient/Flip/Fix winding/Flip normals and the Growth frame. `src/app.rs` `draw_meshes` draws the tab, `draw_cutout_editor` is the Edit Mesh… view, and `render_mesh_preview` draws the 3D preview. Leaves use `meshio::processed_geom` in `gen.rs`.
- Not active yet: Ripple and Proxy collision Scale/Weight are stored only (no wind system or world-building proxies), and "Fronds" in Collection collects nothing (there's no frond generator).

## Still estimated / open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers. The code that applies them reads cached property pointers, not names, so it wasn't found.
2. Phyllotaxy mode reuses the Interval walk; the original's phyllotaxy routine wasn't read.
3. The layout inside the Material and Mesh editors is my design; the original's couldn't be seen without a tree loaded.
4. The original draws randomness from a built-in table, so the same seed won't give an identical tree.
5. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab.
   - Node and Freehand edit modes (buttons shown greyed out).
   - The other six generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent.
   - Property curves (splines).
   - Saving, loading and exporting trees.
   - Wind and LOD export.

## Next steps (in order)
1. **Trace the spine walk.** Follow callers of fn 0x1403154a0 (the per-child evaluator) from the placement routines, or walk the CBranchNode method table in Ghidra, to find where Gravity (property 130) is applied. Replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs` (`make_spine`, `build_spine`).
2. **Add property curves.** Give Frequency, Length and Radius a small curve editor in the Properties panel; the original evaluates these as splines along the parent.
3. **Save and load trees** (a simple JSON file), then add OBJ/FBX export for game engines.
4. **Add the remaining generation modes**, starting with Proportional and Bifurcation (their property names are already known from the templates).
5. **Ask the person for pictures** of the original's Material and Mesh editors, and match their layout.
6. **Add Node and Freehand edit modes** (select and adjust individual branches in the viewport).

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots.
- Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units. The UI scale lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Node templates in `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Modeler v10.2.0\templates\combined\*.stt` are gzip XML holding real defaults.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-08._

## Progress summary
- **Status:** builds and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad. The program is `target/debug/treecraft.exe`; the window is titled "TreeCraft".
- **Built so far:**
  - **Node graph (Generation tab):** Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes with the original's icons. Add, link (Shift+drag), duplicate, hide, delete, randomize, arrange.
  - **Properties panel (left):** shows whatever is clicked (node, material, mesh, window settings), grouped like the original: Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation.
  - **Tree growth:** follows the original's decompiled placement rules for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes. Phyllotaxy is approximate.
  - **Materials tab:**
    - procedural bark and leaf textures, or image files
    - colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours
    - live sphere/card preview
  - **Meshes tab:** matches the original's 8.4.2 Meshes panel (from the person's screenshot and the program's code):
    - drag-to-model handle, mesh picker, +/−, + (OBJ import), Copy/Paste/Duplicate
    - Edit Mesh… cutout editor; High/Med/Low levels with Browse/Reload/Export OBJ; More
    - 3D preview with Alignment guide and V:F count
    - Transform: Orient, Flip, Flip normals, Fix winding
    - Collection: Spines, Pivot
    - Wind direction: Growth, Ripple
    - Proxy collision: Scale, Weight
  - **Viewport:** perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); orbit, pan, zoom, frame, grid; lighting settings; selected node highlighted in orange.
- **Code map (`src/`):**
  - `app.rs`: state, dock tabs, viewport, mesh preview
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
  - `render.rs`: shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: textures and auto-cutout
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Evidence:** every value and its source is in `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json`. Original files used are listed in `CREDITS.md`.
- **Original program now installed:** `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe` (the 10.2 copy studied at first is gone).

## Still open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers: still estimated, because the original's code for this wasn't found.
2. Material editor layout: still my design; a screenshot of the original's would settle it.
3. Stored but not active yet: Ripple and Proxy collision Scale/Weight (no wind or world-building yet). "Fronds" in Collection collects nothing (no frond nodes).
4. The exact axis maths behind each Orient choice is my reading of the labels.
5. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab
   - Node / Freehand edit modes
   - six more generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent
   - property curves
   - save / load / export of whole trees
   - wind

## Next steps (suggested order)
1. Match the Material editor to a screenshot of the original.
2. Save and load trees, then export the whole tree for game engines (OBJ/FBX).
3. Add property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
4. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs`.
5. Add the remaining generation modes and the Node / Freehand edit modes.

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots.
- UI scaling lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`. Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units.
- The original's node templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and tree files (`.spm`) are gzip XML holding real defaults.

input.old_string:
- Transform: Orient (Z-Up Right-handed = 6 default, Y-Up Right-handed 7, Z-Up Left-handed 8,

input.new_string:
- Transform: Orient (Z-Up Right-handed = 6 default, Y-Up Right-handed 7, Z-Up Left-handed 8,
  Y-Up Left-handed 9, XYZ 0, XZY 1, YXZ 2, YZX 3, ZXY 4, ZYX 5), Flip (X Y Z … -X -Y -Z),
  Flip normals, Fix winding.
  - The Orient handler (fn 0x1400823a0, undo text "orient change") stores the choice's value; the Flip
    handler (fn 0x1400822a0, "flip change") stores the list index. Both then reprocess the mesh in
    fn 0x1400ab6c0.
  - Axis matrix per Orient value, read from the switch in fn 0x1400ab6c0 (base matrix = identity at
    0x141796e18). Result (x′, y′, z′) from source (x, y, z):
    | Value | Choice | Result | Mirror |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 0, 6 | XYZ, Z-up RH | (x, y, z) | no |
    | 1, 9 | XZY, Y-up LH | (x, z, y) | yes |
    | 2 | YXZ | (y, x, z) | yes |
    | 3 | YZX | (y, −z, −x) | no |
    | 4 | ZXY | (−z, x, −y) | no |
    | 5 | ZYX | (z, y, x) | yes |
    | 7 | Y-up RH | (x, −z, y) | no |
    | 8 | Z-up LH | (x, y, −z) | yes |
  - Flip index 1/2/3 negates X/Y/Z, 4 = X+Y, 5 = X+Z, 6 = Y+Z, 7 = all three (−1.0 at 0x14102c874).
  - Each mirror and each flipped axis adds one to a count; the faces are reversed when the count is odd.
    Normals go through the same matrix.
  - Wind direction handler (fn 0x14007e100): the wind vector is zeroed, then axis (choice mod 3) is set to
    +1.0 for choices 0–2 or −1.0 for 3–5 (constants 0x1415432f4 = 1.0, 0x14102c874 = −1.0), so the list
    order is +X, +Y, +Z, −X, −Y, −Z.
  - Collision scale and weight have their own handlers (fns 0x14007ddc0 / 0x14007de60).

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-08._

## Progress summary
- **Status:** builds and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad. The program is `target/debug/treecraft.exe`; the window is titled "TreeCraft".
- **Built so far:**
  - **Node graph (Generation tab):** Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes with the original's icons. Add, link (Shift+drag), duplicate, hide, delete, randomize, arrange.
  - **Properties panel (left):** shows whatever is clicked (node, material, mesh, window settings), grouped like the original: Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation.
  - **Tree growth:** follows the original's decompiled placement rules for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes. Phyllotaxy is approximate.
  - **Materials tab:**
    - procedural bark and leaf textures, or image files
    - colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours
    - live sphere/card preview
  - **Meshes tab:** matches the original's 8.4.2 Meshes panel (from the person's screenshot and the program's code):
    - drag-to-model handle, mesh picker, +/−, + (OBJ import), Copy/Paste/Duplicate
    - Edit Mesh… cutout editor; High/Med/Low levels with Browse/Reload/Export OBJ; More
    - 3D preview with Alignment guide and V:F count
    - Transform: Orient, Flip, Flip normals, Fix winding
    - Collection: Spines, Pivot
    - Wind direction: Growth, Ripple
    - Proxy collision: Scale, Weight
  - **Viewport:** perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); orbit, pan, zoom, frame, grid; lighting settings; selected node highlighted in orange.
- **Code map (`src/`):**
  - `app.rs`: state, dock tabs, viewport, mesh preview
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
  - `render.rs`: shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: textures and auto-cutout
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Evidence:** every value and its source is in `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json`. Original files used are listed in `CREDITS.md`.
- **Original program now installed:** `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe` (the 10.2 copy studied at first is gone).

## Still open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers: still estimated, because the original's code for this wasn't found.
2. Material editor layout: still my design; a screenshot of the original's would settle it.
3. Stored but not active yet: Ripple and Proxy collision Scale/Weight (no wind or world-building yet). "Fronds" in Collection collects nothing (no frond nodes).
4. The exact axis maths behind each Orient choice is my reading of the labels.
5. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab
   - Node / Freehand edit modes
   - six more generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent
   - property curves
   - save / load / export of whole trees
   - wind

## Next steps (suggested order)
1. Match the Material editor to a screenshot of the original.
2. Save and load trees, then export the whole tree for game engines (OBJ/FBX).
3. Add property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
4. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs`.
5. Add the remaining generation modes and the Node / Freehand edit modes.

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots.
- UI scaling lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`. Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units.
- The original's node templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and tree files (`.spm`) are gzip XML holding real defaults.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-08._

## Progress summary
- **Status:** builds and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad. The program is `target/debug/treecraft.exe`; the window is titled "TreeCraft".
- **Built so far:**
  - **Node graph (Generation tab):** Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes with the original's icons. Add, link (Shift+drag), duplicate, hide, delete, randomize, arrange.
  - **Properties panel (left):** shows whatever is clicked (node, material, mesh, window settings), grouped like the original: Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation.
  - **Tree growth:** follows the original's decompiled placement rules for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes. Phyllotaxy is approximate.
  - **Materials tab:**
    - procedural bark and leaf textures, or image files
    - colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours
    - live sphere/card preview
  - **Meshes tab:** matches the original's 8.4.2 Meshes panel (from the person's screenshot and the program's code):
    - drag-to-model handle, mesh picker, + (OBJ import), Copy/Paste/Duplicate
    - +/− opens the Meshes dialog (`src/meshdialog.rs`): Add new, Duplicate, Rename (or double-click), Move up/down, Remove, OK/Cancel. Matches the original's CAssetAddRemoveDialog (fn 0x14004e3a0).
    - Edit Mesh… cutout editor; High/Med/Low levels with Browse/Reload/Export OBJ; More
    - 3D preview with Alignment guide and V:F count
    - Transform: Orient, Flip, Flip normals, Fix winding. Orient/Flip use the original's exact axis maths, decompiled from fn 0x1400ab6c0.
    - Collection: Spines, Pivot
    - Wind direction: Growth, Ripple
    - Proxy collision: Scale, Weight
  - **Viewport:** perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); orbit, pan, zoom, frame, grid; lighting settings; selected node highlighted in orange.
- **Code map (`src/`):**
  - `app.rs`: state, dock tabs, viewport, mesh preview
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
  - `render.rs`: shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: textures and auto-cutout
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Evidence:** every value and its source is in `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json`. Original files used are listed in `CREDITS.md`.
- **Original program now installed:** `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe` (the 10.2 copy studied at first is gone).

## Still open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers: still estimated, because the original's code for this wasn't found.
2. Material editor layout: still my design; a screenshot of the original's would settle it.
3. Stored but not active yet: Ripple and Proxy collision Scale/Weight (no wind or world-building yet). "Fronds" in Collection collects nothing (no frond nodes).
4. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab
   - Node / Freehand edit modes
   - six more generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent
   - property curves
   - save / load / export of whole trees
   - wind

## Next steps (suggested order)
1. Match the Material editor to a screenshot of the original.
2. Save and load trees, then export the whole tree for game engines (OBJ/FBX).
3. Add property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
4. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs`.
5. Add the remaining generation modes and the Node / Freehand edit modes.

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots; `TM_DIALOG=1` opens the Meshes dialog at start.
- UI scaling lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`. Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units.
- Mesh-panel decompiles: the change handlers (fns 0x1400823a0 orient, 0x1400822a0 flip, 0x14007e100 wind) lead to the processing code. The file loader fn 0x1400b19b0 is too big for Ghidra.
- The original's node templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and tree files (`.spm`) are gzip XML holding real defaults.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-09._

## Progress summary
- **Status:** builds and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test also drives the Meshes dialog (add, duplicate, rename, reorder, OK).
- **Stack:** Rust + macroquad. The program is `target/debug/treecraft.exe`; the window is titled "TreeCraft".
- **Built so far:**
  - **Node graph (Generation tab):** Tree / Trunk / Branch / Leaf nodes with the original's icons. Add, link (Shift+drag), duplicate, hide, delete, randomize, arrange.
  - **Properties panel (left):** shows whatever is clicked (node, material, mesh, window settings), grouped like the original: Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation.
  - **Tree growth:** follows the original's decompiled placement rules for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes. Phyllotaxy is approximate.
  - **Materials tab:**
    - procedural bark and leaf textures, or image files
    - colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours
    - live sphere/card preview
  - **Meshes tab:** matches the original's 8.4.2 Meshes panel (from the person's screenshot and the program's code):
    - drag-to-model handle, mesh picker, + (OBJ import), Copy/Paste/Duplicate
    - +/− opens the Meshes dialog (`src/meshdialog.rs`): Add new, Duplicate, Rename (or double-click), Move up/down, Remove, OK/Cancel. Matches the original's CAssetAddRemoveDialog (fn 0x14004e3a0).
    - Edit Mesh… cutout editor; High/Med/Low levels with Browse/Reload/Export OBJ; More
    - 3D preview with Alignment guide and V:F count
    - Transform: Orient, Flip, Flip normals, Fix winding. Orient, Flip, Flip normals and Fix winding follow the original's mesh processing exactly (fn 0x1400ab6c0: axis matrices, odd-count face reversal, the 90° winding rule, degenerate-face removal).
    - Collection: Spines, Pivot
    - Wind direction: Growth, Ripple
    - Proxy collision: Scale, Weight
  - **Viewport:** perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); orbit, pan, zoom, frame, grid; lighting settings; selected node highlighted in orange.
- **Code map (`src/`):**
  - `app.rs`: state, dock tabs, viewport, mesh preview
  - `props.rs`: Properties panel
  - `gen.rs`: tree growth
  - `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
  - `meshdialog.rs`: the Meshes add/remove/rename dialog
  - `render.rs`: shader and camera
  - `textures.rs`: textures and auto-cutout
  - `model.rs`: data types
  - `ui.rs`: the user-interface toolkit
  - `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`
- **Evidence:** every value and its source is in `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json`. Original files used are listed in `CREDITS.md`.
- **Original program now installed:** `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe` (the 10.2 copy studied at first is gone).

## Still open
1. How branches bend (gravity, noise, jink) and how the radius tapers: still estimated, because the original's code for this wasn't found.
2. Material editor layout: still my design; a screenshot of the original's would settle it.
3. Stored but not active yet: Ripple and Proxy collision Scale/Weight (no wind or world-building yet). "Fronds" in Collection collects nothing (no frond nodes).
4. Not built yet:
   - Displacements tab
   - Node / Freehand edit modes
   - six more generation modes: Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent
   - property curves
   - save / load / export of whole trees
   - wind

## Next steps (suggested order)
1. Match the Material editor to a screenshot of the original.
2. Save and load trees, then export the whole tree for game engines (OBJ/FBX).
3. Add property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
4. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimated bend and taper in `gen.rs`.
5. Add the remaining generation modes and the Node / Freehand edit modes.

## Useful tricks
- `TM_TAB=0..2` and `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N` set a start state for screenshots; `TM_DIALOG=1` opens the Meshes dialog at start.
- UI scaling lives in `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`. Macroquad reports sizes in display-scaled units.
- Mesh-panel decompiles: the change handlers (fns 0x1400823a0 orient, 0x1400822a0 flip, 0x14007e100 wind) lead to the processing code. The file loader fn 0x1400b19b0 is too big for Ghidra.
- The original's node templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and tree files (`.spm`) are gzip XML holding real defaults.

I decompiled the rest of the original's Meshes panel and changed four things to match it:
- **Duplicate:** the copy is now named "… Copy" (with the original's numbering when that name is taken) and added at the end of the list.
- **Loading a file over a cutout:** you're now asked first whether you really want to replace the mesh's own data.
- **Loading a High file:** TreeCraft now offers to find matching "…LOD1", "…LOD2" files in the same folder and fill Med and Low with them. It only reads OBJ files; the original also looks for its other mesh formats.
- **Count label:** it now reads like the original's, for example "V:27  F:32  A:1".

One difference remains: in the original, Edit Mesh… on a mesh loaded from a file converts it so it can be edited. TreeCraft can only edit cutouts, so it offers "Replace with a cutout" instead.

These rules are in the values sheet. A new test checks the LOD file search, and the app builds and passes Craft Anything's check.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N".
