tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_capture_show
tools.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus counts by model. decoders limits decoding to those protocol numbers (see radio_decoders_list); otherwise rtl_433's default set runs. Optional engine.

The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it lists and check again before replying. Not counted as a round. project defaults to the project this tool server works for.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_question_ask
tools.description: Ask a question about a project's build ("where are the latest files?", "why this engine?") without starting a build or a round, and without changing anything. Claude Code answers from a copy of the builder's own session, which isn't kept, reading files only (none in Clean room); an AI with an API key answers with the tools that change nothing. Other coding agents are refused. Safe while a build runs: it doesn't interrupt it. Returns the answer, how it was answered and its cost, and keeps it in the project (`rebuild_questions_list`).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_start
tools.description: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start on their own as others finish. It runs a coding agent that writes and builds code, so it needs consent.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_start
schema.description: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start on their own as others finish. It runs a coding agent that writes and builds code, so it needs consent.

backend.description:
The coding agent to use (an enabled backend name), kept with a new project for its later
changes; default: the one set up for building.

build_with.description: What to build with: an engine (unity, unreal, godot, rust) or a stack's full name.

existing.description:
With `project_folder` that has files: `edit` (they're the app, edited in place) or
`start_from` (material to start from; the app is built in app/ beside them).

generate_assets.description:
For a new game: the builder may generate pictures and 3D models (paid from the person's
asset provider key, within the project's budget). Default false; change it later with
project_assets_allow.

pictures.description:
Pictures of the original (absolute paths): the look the person expects. They're copied
into the project's reference/ folder for the builder.

project.description: Continue this project folder instead of starting a new one.

project_folder.description:
Start the new project in this folder itself instead (it's added to the project list). If
it already has files, `existing` says what they are.

projects_dir.description: Where a new project's folder goes (default: the projects folder from settings).

request.description: What to make (a new project), or the follow-up message (with `project`).

resume.description:
With `project`: carry on where its last run stopped (paused, or the app or the computer
stopped) instead of sending `request` as a follow-up.

rounds.description: Refinement rounds after the first build (default 2).

target.description: For a new project: a web address, an absolute path to an app, game or file, or `-` for none.

ExistingFiles.description: What the files already in a picked folder are to a new project.

oneOf.description: The app itself: the builder edits them in place.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_read
tools.description: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters. Other hosts get a clear wrong_os result.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_read
schema.description: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters. Other hosts get a clear wrong_os result.

max_nodes.description: Largest number of accessibility nodes to return.

pid.description: The process id of the running app.

screenshot.description:
Include a screenshot (PNG, base64) alongside the tree. macOS 14+: captures one on-screen
window belonging to pid, restricted by window_id when supplied, at up to 2048 pixels
per side. Without window_id, captures the first matching window. Needs existing Screen
Recording permission; failures are explicit limitations and never open permission dialogs.

window_id.description: A specific window to restrict to (on Windows, its window handle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Each step names an action and an element (its exact title or identifier). macOS: any accessibility action (e.g. AXPress). Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. Each step reports dispatched, element_not_found, not_supported, unknown_action or failed. Password fields' titles and values are never read. Other hosts get wrong_os.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_walkthrough_record
schema.description: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. Each step reports dispatched, element_not_found, not_supported, unknown_action or failed. Password fields' titles and values are never read. Other hosts get wrong_os.

steps.description: Steps to perform, each an accessibility action such as press/focus on an element path.

action.description:
Accessibility action, e.g. `AXPress` (on Windows also press, expand, collapse, toggle,

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
schema.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

environment.description: Extra environment variables applied on top of the inherited environment.

executable.description: The program to run (absolute path or a name resolved on PATH).

finish_ms.description: 0 = SIGKILL at the deadline; > 0 = SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

normalization.description:
Make two runs comparable: replace values that change every run (on by default for process
ids, ports and 10 ms time buckets).

sandbox.description: Run inside bubblewrap if it is installed (recorded honestly either way).

watched_paths.description:
Absolute paths to snapshot before and after (opt-in). File contents are never read; only
path, size and sha256.

working_directory.description: Working directory (absolute). Defaults to the program's own default.

data.description: Text to type. A trailing newline is not added for you.

paths.description: Replace the working directory and the temp folder with <cwd> and <tmp>.

patterns.description: Literal replacements (no patterns), applied last; at most 100.

pids.description: Replace the run's process ids with <pid>.

ports.description: Replace ports after localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and [::1] with <port>.

time_step_ms.description: Round event dispatch times down to this many milliseconds (0 keeps them exact).

tools.description: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pixels_compare
schema.description: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

before.description: Earlier PNG: a web_page_screenshot_take evidence (inline/retained), or inline {base64} / {path}.

common_area.description:
Compare the area both images share (top-left) when their sizes differ, and add a coarse
`layout_similarity` (0..1, share of 16 px tiles with matching mean colour) and a
`perceptual_similarity` (0..1, mean SSIM of brightness: edges, text, texture). Use it to
compare a rebuild with the original page, whose heights rarely match exactly.

ignore.description:
With common_area: a noise-<width>.png mask from web_site_capture ({path} or {base64});
its white squares (parts that change by themselves) are left out of the layout and detail.

tolerance.description: Per-channel difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed (0..=255).

tools.description: Answer HTTP requests on this computer from a file written by web_standin_build, and return its URL to point a rebuilt front end at. tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a scripted browser session (goto/click/fill/press/select/wait; elements by CSS selector, test_id, or role and accessible name; optional step_id per step) over CDP, attaching to a loopback endpoint or launching a located Chromium. A fixed environment (viewport, locale, time zone, colour scheme, reduced motion, service workers; 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light by default) makes runs repeatable. Captures per-step network request outlines and optional screenshots; keep_bodies can also keep request/response bodies and header values (off by default, credentials and declared secrets redacted). storage can start the run with cookies and local/session storage (values treated as secrets). capture records screenshot, DOM, accessibility tree, history and storage key names after each step and/or at the end. capture.events records console, page errors, WebSockets, frames, workers, popups and (blocked) downloads, each tagged with its step. Executes page interactions and accesses the network, so it needs your approval; declared secrets are redacted in every encoding and bodies are reduced to outlines.

content.text:
I rebuilt the Materials tab to match your screenshots, and it builds and passes all the checks:

1. **Texture slots:** the ten slots (Color, Opacity, Normal, Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, Subsurface%, AO, Custom) each have a colour or number, an on/off tick and a picture box. Click a box to load an image; right-click to clear it.
2. **Top buttons:** +/- opens a Materials window to add, duplicate, rename, reorder and remove materials. + picks texture files and makes a new material for each one. The clipboard button has Copy, Paste and Duplicate.
3. **Meshes sub-tab:** it sits next to Settings, with Unwrap, an Add button, and rows where you pick a mesh for the material, with buttons to edit or show that mesh.

Right now only the Color, Opacity and Normal pictures change how the tree looks; images in the other slots are saved but don't show yet. I couldn't find what "Make New Set..." does in the original, so for now it makes a copy of the material.

-  - **Properties panel (left):** shows whatever is clicked (node, material, mesh, window settings), grouped like the original: Generation, Spine, Skin, Segments, Materials, Leaves, Local Orientation, Deformation.
-  - **Tree growth:** follows the original's decompiled placement rules for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes. Phyllotaxy is approximate.
-    - procedural bark and leaf textures, or image files
-    - colour adjustments, opacity cutoff, bump, gloss, specular, metallic, subsurface, AO, variation colours
-  - **Meshes tab:** matches the original's 8.4.2 Meshes panel (from the person's screenshot and the program's code):
-    - drag-to-model handle, mesh picker, + (OBJ import), Copy/Paste/Duplicate

-    - +/− opens the Meshes dialog (`src/meshdialog.rs`): Add new, Duplicate, Rename (or double-click), Move up/down, Remove, OK/Cancel. Matches the original's CAssetAddRemoveDialog (fns 0x14004e3a0, 0x1405ff5d0, 0x1400509b0, 0x1400860d0):

-      - Add new makes an empty "Mesh" (no High/Med/Low, blank preview) with the original's starting settings (fn 0x1400b1000): Growth +Y, Ripple Normal, Orient Z-Up Right-handed, Flip X Y Z, collision scale and weight 1, More none.
-      - Duplicate makes "<name> Copy" at the end and opens it for renaming.
-      - The arrows move every selected mesh.
-    - Edit Mesh… cutout editor; High/Med/Low levels with Browse/Reload/Export OBJ; More
-    - 3D preview with Alignment guide and V:F count

-    - Transform: Orient, Flip, Flip normals, Fix winding. Orient, Flip, Flip normals and Fix winding follow the original's mesh processing exactly (fn 0x1400ab6c0: axis matrices, odd-count face reversal, the 90° winding rule, degenerate-face removal).
-  - **Viewport:** perspective by default; Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom views (orthographic); orbit, pan, zoom, frame, grid; lighting settings; selected node highlighted in orange.
-  - `app.rs`: state, dock tabs, viewport, mesh preview
-- **Evidence:** every value and its source is in `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json`. Original files used are listed in `CREDITS.md`.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (90 values: 75 sourced, 15 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, the node graph, the Properties panel, the Materials panel parts, the Meshes tab and the Meshes window.

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate).
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab:** matches the original's panel (person's picture-1..3 plus code): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files, cutout editor, Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6): picker, +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, preview, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots. New-material defaults come from the original's constructor. "Make New Set..." follows the original: it adds a "<name> Set" material whose one member is the current material (weight 1.0).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; Gloss/Specular/Metallic/Subsurface/Subsurface%/AO/Custom pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (editing members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (open unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6).
4. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds"; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
5. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader and camera
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.

## Useful tricks
- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window) or `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window).
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- The original's templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and trees (`.spm`) are gzip XML with real defaults.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.

1	# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)
2	
3	_Last updated 2026-11-10 (pictures 7-8 done)._
4	
5	## Project
6	- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
7	- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
8	- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (90 values: 75 sourced, 15 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.
9	
10	## Status
11	Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, the node graph, the Properties panel, the Materials panel parts, the Meshes tab and the Meshes window.
12	
13	## Done
14	- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate).
15	- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
16	- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
17	- **Meshes tab:** matches the original's panel (person's picture-1..3 plus code): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files, cutout editor, Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code.
18	- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6): picker, +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, preview, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots. New-material defaults come from the original's constructor. "Make New Set..." follows the original: it adds a "<name> Set" material whose one member is the current material (weight 1.0).
19	
20	- **Pictures 7-8:** Meshes tab preview is wireframe by default with a Wireframe/Material switch; New tree clears all materials, textures and meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout); material preview shapes Sphere, Plane, Cylinder, Custom... (any OBJ); the preview turns only when dragged (double-click resets).
21	
22	## Outstanding
23	1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; Gloss/Specular/Metallic/Subsurface/Subsurface%/AO/Custom pictures are stored only.
24	2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (editing members and weights) isn't built.
25	3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (open unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6).
26	4. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds"; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
27	5. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.
28	
29	## Important files (`app/src/`)
...
40	## Next tasks
41	1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
42	2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
43	3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
44	4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
45	5. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.
46	
47	## Useful tricks
48	- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window) or `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window), `TM_NEW=1` (start as after File > New tree).
49	- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
50	- The original's templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and trees (`.spm`) are gzip XML with real defaults.
51	- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10 (pictures 7-8 done)._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (94 values: 78 sourced, 16 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, the node graph, the Properties panel, the Materials panel parts, the Meshes tab and the Meshes window.

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate).
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab:** matches the original's panel (person's picture-1..3 plus code): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files, cutout editor, Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6): picker, +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, preview, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots. New-material defaults come from the original's constructor. "Make New Set..." follows the original: it adds a "<name> Set" material whose one member is the current material (weight 1.0). The picker hides sets; the Meshes sub-tab's first row is the cutout mesh (fn 0x140068ed0).
- **Pictures 7-8:** Meshes tab preview is wireframe by default with a Wireframe/Material switch; New tree clears all materials, textures and meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout); material preview shapes Sphere, Plane, Cylinder, Custom... (any OBJ); the preview turns only when dragged (double-click resets).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; Gloss/Specular/Metallic/Subsurface/Subsurface%/AO/Custom pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (editing members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (open unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6).
4. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds"; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
5. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader and camera
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Trace the original's branch-bending code and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.

## Useful tricks
- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window) or `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window), `TM_NEW=1` (start as after File > New tree).
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- The original's templates (`templates\combined\*.stt`) and trees (`.spm`) are gzip XML with real defaults.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.

content.text:
I looked into how the original bends branches. The part that bends a branch step by step still wasn't found, but I did confirm what "Jink" means. In the original, Jink is a separate "early" noise whose frequency is set as 1 minus a threshold value, and its default trunk and branch files give a frequency of 0.5.

TreeCraft now has a "Jink frequency" setting next to Jink, starting at the original's 0.5. Before, a fixed 0.25 was used, which was my guess. Jink itself still starts at 0, as in the original, so default trees look the same. The build passes every check.

How gravity and the other noise curve a branch at each step, and how branches narrow toward the tip, are still my estimates. The handoff names the next function to read for that.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (105 values: 88 sourced, 17 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, node graph, Properties panel, Materials panel, Meshes tab and Meshes window (not the Edit Cutout window).

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate). Jink frequency setting (default 0.5) from the original's rules.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab** (pictures 1-3, 7): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files ("Embedded" label for embedded meshes), Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code; preview is wireframe by default with a Material switch and a right-click Lit/Scribed menu.
- **Edit Cutout window** (picture 9): Edit Mesh... warns before embedding a file-based mesh, then opens a modal window with Points, Anchors, Material, Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), the canvas and High/Med/Low with arrows; only Confirm/Cancel close it. No masks: outlines can't cross themselves.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's new-material defaults, Make New Set... per the original. Preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom (OBJ); turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; the other slot pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). Next candidate to read: fn 0x140196510.
4. Estimated behaviour: what Tessellation and the Angle thumb wheel (turns the growth line) do to the mesh (their controls and the Load/Save arrows are confirmed from code), "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Missing: Cull backfaces and Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds", extra anchors; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
6. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `cutout.rs`: Edit Cutout window
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader, camera, preview shapes
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files, cutout geometry and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Read fn 0x140196510 for the branch-bending rules and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.
6. Add an Edit Cutout step to the self-test.

## Useful tricks
- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window), `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window), `TM_DIALOG=cut` (Edit Cutout window), `TM_NEW=1` (as after File > New tree).
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Real defaults live in the install's gzip XML files: `app_data\sketch\trunk.stt` / `branch.stt` and the `.spm` trees.
- If an open TreeCraft window locks `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, rename the file and rebuild; `treecraft-running-old.exe` there is such a leftover and can be removed once no copy is running.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.
- In PowerShell use absolute paths with `[IO.File]` calls (its working folder differs from PowerShell's).

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (105 values: 88 sourced, 17 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, node graph, Properties panel, Materials panel, Meshes tab and Meshes window (not the Edit Cutout window).

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate). Jink frequency setting (default 0.5) from the original's rules.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab** (pictures 1-3, 7): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files ("Embedded" label for embedded meshes), Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code; preview is wireframe by default with a Material switch and a right-click Lit/Scribed menu.
- **Edit Cutout window** (picture 9): Edit Mesh... warns before embedding a file-based mesh, then opens a modal window with Points, Anchors, Material, Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), the canvas and High/Med/Low with arrows; only Confirm/Cancel close it. No masks: outlines can't cross themselves.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's new-material defaults, Make New Set... per the original. Preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom (OBJ); turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; the other slot pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). fns 0x140192780 and 0x140196510 are ruled out (old-file converters); next, find the vtable holding fn 0x1403154a0 and read its neighbours.
4. Estimated behaviour: what Tessellation and the Angle thumb wheel (turns the growth line) do to the mesh (their controls and the Load/Save arrows are confirmed from code), "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Missing: Cull backfaces and Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds", extra anchors; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
6. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `cutout.rs`: Edit Cutout window
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader, camera, preview shapes
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files, cutout geometry and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Read fn 0x140196510 for the branch-bending rules and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.
6. Add an Edit Cutout step to the self-test.

## Useful tricks
- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window), `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window), `TM_DIALOG=cut` (Edit Cutout window), `TM_NEW=1` (as after File > New tree).
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Real defaults live in the install's gzip XML files: `app_data\sketch\trunk.stt` / `branch.stt` and the `.spm` trees.
- If an open TreeCraft window locks `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, rename the file and rebuild; `treecraft-running-old.exe` there is such a leftover and can be removed once no copy is running.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.
- In PowerShell use absolute paths with `[IO.File]` calls (its working folder differs from PowerShell's).

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (105 values: 88 sourced, 17 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, node graph, Properties panel, Materials panel, Meshes tab and Meshes window (not the Edit Cutout window).

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate). Jink frequency setting (default 0.5) from the original's rules.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab** (pictures 1-3, 7): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files ("Embedded" label for embedded meshes), Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code; preview is wireframe by default with a Material switch and a right-click Lit/Scribed menu.
- **Edit Cutout window** (picture 9): Edit Mesh... warns before embedding a file-based mesh, then opens a modal window with Points, Anchors, Material, Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), the canvas and High/Med/Low with arrows; only Confirm/Cancel close it. No masks: outlines can't cross themselves.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's new-material defaults, Make New Set... per the original. Preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom (OBJ); turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; the other slot pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). Ruled out: fns 0x140192780 and 0x140196510 (old-file converters) and fn 0x1403154a0 (image processing). Next: find code reading the Spine:Shape:Gravity property (index 130) from the branch node.
4. Estimated behaviour: what Tessellation and the Angle thumb wheel (turns the growth line) do to the mesh (their controls and the Load/Save arrows are confirmed from code), "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Missing: Cull backfaces and Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds", extra anchors; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
6. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `cutout.rs`: Edit Cutout window
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader, camera, preview shapes
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files, cutout geometry and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).

I made all four cutout editor changes, and TreeCraft builds and passes every check.

1. **Clean start:** a mesh with no cutout now opens with no points, and "Reset points" clears back to nothing.
2. **No automatic subdivision:** the mesh is no longer split up on its own; only the Tessellation option adds detail. Leaves on the tree now use about a third as many triangles.
3. **Move and resize:** drag the title bar to move the window and the bottom-right corner to resize it, or double-click the title to fill the TreeCraft window. It remembers its size and place. It can't go onto another monitor, though: TreeCraft runs as a single window, so the editor stays inside it.
4. **Anchor and angle:** a new Anchor group has X, Y and Angle controls. You can also drag the white anchor with the normal point tool, and drag an orange knob on the growth line to turn the angle.

brief.question: Rebuild the core of the tree modeler: a node graph (Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf generators), properties panel on the left, material editor, mesh editor, and a 3D viewport with perspective and orthographic views — no presets.

findings.statement: Generator 'Generation:Mode' choices in order: Classic, Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute, Absolute steps, Phyllotaxy, Interval, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent (built in function 0x1403175a0). Node templates (gzip XML .stt) give the property groups and defaults: Trunk = Absolute 1, Spine length 25, radius 1, start angle 0.5; Branch = length 40% of parent, radius 66% of parent, start angle 0.35, first 0.215 last 0.925; Leaf size 1.

Classic placement (fn 0x140477e40): count = trunc(Frequency) or trunc(parentLength × Frequency × 0.025) in Relative style; positions random between First and Last weighted by the frequency curve (fn 0x1402cad40); roll in turns = (Balanced ? i/n : random) + random(±Offset)×0.5, ×Sweep, +Roll. Absolute (fn 0x1404723f0) uses i/n + ±Jumble/2, centred. Interval (fn 0x14047b6f0) steps down from Last by 10/Frequency length units with Count children per node and Spiral×0.1 turns per node.

Property limits come from static tables (spine fn 0x14053b8c0, skin fn 0x140540c10): Start angle 0..1, Orientation Roll −1..1, Gravity unbounded, Straightness and Jink amount 0..1, Radial segments 0..100000 (suggested 3), Radius % of parent suggested 0.75, Length kill ratio 500.

The original's Meshes panel (8.4.2, fn 0x140076fd0 / 0x140084750) has: drag handle, mesh picker, +/- (manage), + (browse & add), Copy/Paste/Duplicate; Geometry with Edit Mesh..., High/Med/Low files (Browse, Reload, Export) and More; Show (LOD) + Alignment + V:F count; Transform (Orient: Z-Up RH=6, Y-Up RH=7, Z-Up LH=8, Y-Up LH=9, XYZ..ZYX=0..5; Flip: 8 sign combinations; Flip normals; Fix winding); Collection (Spines: Branches/Fronds/Both; Pivot: Origin/First); Wind direction (Growth ±X/±Y/±Z; Ripple Normal/X/Y/Z); Proxy collision (Scale, Weight).

Mesh processing (fn 0x1400ab6c0, 8.4.2) applies an axis matrix per Orient value: 0/6 identity, 1/9 (x,z,y), 2 (y,x,z), 3 (y,−z,−x), 4 (−z,x,−y), 5 (z,y,x), 7 (x,−z,y), 8 (x,y,−z). Flip index 1–7 negates X/Y/Z combinations. Faces reverse when mirrors + flips is odd. The Wind-direction handler (fn 0x14007e100) sets the wind axis to choice mod 3 with sign + for 0–2, − for 3–5.

Mesh processing (fn 0x1400ab6c0, 8.4.2): Flip normals negates normals and counts toward the face-reversal parity. Faces with cross product length² < 1e-12 are dropped. Vertex normals with length² < 0.9 get face normals × 0.01 added. Fix winding swaps a face when its winding normal is more than 90° from its vertex normals.

The original's Meshes dialog (CAssetAddRemoveDialog; +/- handler fn 0x1400860d0, slots in fn 0x1405ff5d0, naming fn 0x1400509b0): title "Meshes", default name "Mesh". Duplicate appends "<name> Copy" at the end and opens it for renaming. Move up/down shift all selected items. Rename edits the first selected item. Remove deletes all selected. A taken name has its trailing number incremented or " 2" appended. Changes apply only on OK, and the panel keeps its previous mesh.

New meshes in the original (fn 0x1400b1000, 8.4.2) start with:
- three empty levels
- wind (0,1,0) = Growth +Y, ripple-is-normal on with direction (0,0,1)
- Flip 0, Orient 6 (Z-Up RH)
- collision scale 1 and weight 1
- Fix winding and Flip normals off, More −1

TreeCraft's LeafMesh::empty uses the same defaults.

Meshes panel handlers (dispatcher fn 0x1406003e0, 8.4.2):
- Paste keeps the current mesh's name and id.
- Duplicate makes a unique "<name> Copy" at the end and selects it.
- Browse warns before replacing embedded data.
- Loading High offers an LOD search: strip trailing digits and "lod", then take later "<base>lod<n>" files in name order.
- The count label is "V:%1  F:%2" plus "  A:%1" for anchors.

Make New Set... (fn 0x14006d8c0) appends a new default material named "<current> Set" (made unique by fn 0x1400af740), flags it as a material set and gives it one member: the current material with weight 1.0. The material constructor (fn 0x1400a7390) sets slot defaults Gloss 0.25, Specular 0.75 grey, AO 1, Color/Opacity/Normal/Subsurface 1, Custom black, and variation colours 0.28/0.37/0.00, 0.59/0.72/0.32, 0.46/0.55/0.46.

The Materials panel refresh (fn 0x140068ed0) lists only non-set materials in the picker. Its Meshes sub-tab shows 1 + supplemental-mesh rows: row 0 is the material's cutout mesh, with a disabled, blank delete button, and the other rows have "X" delete buttons. Each row has Edit... (GenerateMesh) and a go-to button (GoToMesh). The Variation Amount slider position is Amount² × 10000 (constant 0x141031c10).

The shared preview widget never turns on its own; it moves only with mouse input. Setting a material (fn 0x1402ec790) or resetting the view (fn 0x1402ecdd0) puts the angles back to -π/2 and -1.728 rad and the zoom to 0. The wheel (fn 0x1402ece70) adds delta × -0.001 to the zoom, i.e. 0.12 per notch. Right-clicking a mesh preview (fn 0x1402ecb70) offers the check items Lit, Cull backfaces, Scribed and Show unique uvs.

The original's old-file converter (fn 0x140192780) maps Jink amount to Early noise Amount and Jink frequency to Early noise Threshold = 1 − frequency, and maps Disturbance to Late noise Amount × 1.5. The install's default trunk/branch templates set Early Threshold 0.5 and Amount 0, so the build's Jink frequency defaults to 0.5.

Edit Mesh... (fn 0x1400828d0) warns "Editing this mesh will convert it to embedded…" only for meshes that aren't embedded yet: No cancels; Yes embeds the mesh and opens the Edit Cutout window. The window (fns 0x1402fc9c0, 0x1402f32a0) has Points, Anchors, Mask and Color (both masks paint triangles away), Material (Show color, Show opacity, Show all meshes) and Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding) groups, plus High/Med/Low panels each with two arrows and a v/f count.

In the Edit Cutout window (COptimalMeshDialog, fns 0x1402f4120 and 0x1402f83f0), Tessellation is a slider from 0 to 10000 (page step 100) and Angle is a thumb wheel (CThumbWheel, fn 0x140409be0, step 2). Each level's first button is LoadButton and its second is SaveButton. The canvas and level column start at 600:100 in a splitter. The original's help for the matching option in its Simplify dialog (fn 0x14033b570) says Improve folding adds a center point to the mesh.

In the Edit Cutout window (dispatcher fn 0x1406038b0), Reset Points (fn 0x1402f7c90) and Reset Anchors (fn 0x1402f8270) each first ask a Yes/No question ending "This cannot be undone". On Yes they reset the canvas (fns 0x140301210, 0x1403013f0) and switch to Add points (mode 0) or Add anchors (mode 4).

lines: - Window title "Edit Cutout - <mesh>" (fn 0x1402fc9c0). Parts and tooltips (fn 0x1402f32a0): Points (Add/Move points, Remove points, Reset points), Anchors (three buttons), Mask (Paint mask to remove triangles, Erase mask, Reset mask), Color (Paint mask to remove triangles, colour, Reset mask), Material (combo, Show color, Show opacity, Show all meshes), Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), High/Med/Low each with two arrow buttons and "v: f:".

- The build leaves out Mask and Color at the person's request; instead an outline can't be made to cross itself, so concave shapes triangulate without overlap. Confirm / Cancel (the person's request) are the only way to close the window.

- Controls (fns 0x1402f4120, 0x1402f83f0, class COptimalMeshDialog): Tessellation is a QSlider 0..10000, page step 100 (0..1 in the build); Angle is a CThumbWheel (fn 0x140409be0; the window sets its step to 2) sending AngleChanged; Double-sided and Improve folding are check boxes. Per level, the first arrow is LoadButton and the second SaveButton: load = edit that level in the window, save = put the window's shape into that level (as built). The canvas and the level column start at 600:100 in a splitter. The (unbuilt) mask colour defaults to red (QColor 7).

-- At the person's request (picture-11): a new point is inserted next to the closest existing point (on the side that keeps the outline simple and adds the shorter edge). The first anchor is the Pivot (white, orange angle line: where the leaf attaches and grows). Other anchors are green, each with its own angle line (degrees clockwise from up in the picture). A Leaf generator placed under a Leaf generator spawns one leaf on each green anchor of each parent leaf, pointing along that anchor's line (its Start angle starts at 0; Roll turns it around the line; size, droop, twist etc. come from its own properties). The anchors go through the same Pivot angle, Orient, Flip, Scale, leaf size and fold as the mesh (curl is applied to position only). This follows the person's design, and the original confirms the shape of it: when a generator's parent is a mesh with anchors, the placement routine (fn 0x1402456e0) skips the generation modes and asks the parent mesh to place children on its anchors (filtered by the generator's First/Last and its "Generation:Anchors" choice); if none were placed it reports "Unable to find anchor for node (check mesh anchors (including LOD meshes), first/last, and anchor restrictions)". "Generation:Anchors" (fn 0x14024b880, next to Generation:Mode) offers All anchors, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The build has the Anchors choice on Leaf generators and shows that message in the status bar; how First/Last filter anchors isn't read, so they don't filter anchors in the build.

- Slots (COptimalMeshDialog meta-object, dispatcher fn 0x1406038b0, in order): IntChanged, AngleChanged, SpinnerChange, Other, ModeAddPoints (fn 0x1402f7b30), ModeRemovePoints, ResetPoints (fn 0x1402f7c90), ModeAddMask, ModeRemoveMask, ResetMask, ModeColor, ColorClicked, ColorChanged, ResetColor, ModeAddAnchors (fn 0x1402f8110), ModeRemoveAnchors, ResetAnchors (fn 0x1402f8270), ColorTypeChanged, MaterialChanged, SaveButton, LoadButton, TimerFirstShow, UpdatePreviews.

- Reset Points (fn 0x1402f7c90) asks "Are you sure you wish to reset the points? This cannot be undone" (title "Reset Points", Yes/No); Yes resets the canvas (fn 0x140301210) and switches to Add points (mode 0). Reset Anchors (fn 0x1402f8270) asks "Are you sure you wish to reset the Anchors? This cannot be undone" and then switches to Add anchors (mode 4; canvas reset fn 0x1403013f0). Both clear the generated mesh. The canvas reset of points leaves one entry at (0.5, 0.25, 0) (constants 0x1415433a0, 0x141543440) whose role isn't settled; the build clears the outline (clean slate, the person's request) and resets anchors to (0.5, 1.0).

- Improve folding: the original's help for the same option in its Simplify dialog (fn 0x14033b570) says it adds a center point to the mesh, which helps folding; the build adds one vertex at the outline's centroid.

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (105 values: 88 sourced, 17 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). The self-test covers the camera, node graph, Properties panel, Materials panel, Meshes tab and Meshes window (not the Edit Cutout window).

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate). Jink frequency setting (default 0.5) from the original's rules.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective and orthographic views, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab** (pictures 1-3, 7): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files ("Embedded" label for embedded meshes), Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original's code; preview is wireframe by default with a Material switch and a right-click Lit/Scribed menu.
- **Edit Cutout window** (picture 9): Edit Mesh... warns before embedding a file-based mesh, then opens a modal window with Points, Anchors, Material, Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), the canvas and High/Med/Low with arrows; only Confirm/Cancel close it. No masks: outlines can't cross themselves.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's new-material defaults, Make New Set... per the original. Preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom (OBJ); turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

- **Picture 10 (Edit Cutout):** opens with no points for a mesh without a cutout, no automatic subdivision (Tessellation only), window moves/resizes inside the app (remembered), Anchor group (X, Y, Angle) and an angle knob on the orange growth line. It can't leave the TreeCraft window for another monitor (one OS window only).

- **Picture 11:** new points join the closest point; first anchor = Pivot (white, orange line); green anchors with their own angle lines; a Leaf generator under a Leaf generator spawns leaves on the parent leaves' green anchors (`gen.rs` ParentRef::Anchor, `meshio::anchor_points`). Unit tests: `cargo test`.

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; the other slot pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). Ruled out: fns 0x140192780 and 0x140196510 (old-file converters) and fn 0x1403154a0 (image processing). Next: find code reading the Spine:Shape:Gravity property (index 130) from the branch node.
4. Estimated behaviour: what Tessellation and the Angle thumb wheel (turns the growth line) do to the mesh (their controls and the Load/Save arrows are confirmed from code), "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Missing: Cull backfaces and Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds", extra anchors; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
6. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind.

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab
- `cutout.rs`: Edit Cutout window
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader, camera, preview shapes
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files, cutout geometry and mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader in `render.rs`.
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0) to edit set members and weights.
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Find the original's branch-bending code (see Outstanding 3) and replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.
6. Add an Edit Cutout step to the self-test.

## Useful tricks
- Start-state variables for screenshots: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1` (Materials Meshes sub-tab), `TM_DIALOG=1` (Meshes window), `TM_DIALOG=mat` (Materials window), `TM_DIALOG=cut` (Edit Cutout window), `TM_NEW=1` (as after File > New tree).
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Real defaults live in the install's gzip XML files: `app_data\sketch\trunk.stt` / `branch.stt` and the `.spm` trees.
- If an open TreeCraft window locks `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, rename the file and rebuild; `treecraft-running-old.exe` there is such a leftover and can be removed once no copy is running.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.
- In PowerShell use absolute paths with `[IO.File]` calls (its working folder differs from PowerShell's).

- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; placement follows the original for Classic, Absolute and Interval modes (Phyllotaxy approximate). Jink frequency setting (default 0.5) from the original's rules.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.

- **Edit Cutout window** (picture 9): Edit Mesh... warns before embedding a file-based mesh, then opens a modal window with Points, Anchors, Material, Options (Tessellation, Angle, Double-sided, Improve folding), the canvas and High/Med/Low with arrows; only Confirm/Cancel close it. No masks: outlines can't cross themselves.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- Materials window, + makes materials from texture files, copy/paste menu, Settings and Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's new-material defaults, Make New Set... per the original. Preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom (OBJ); turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree still has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

- **Picture 10 (Edit Cutout):** opens with no points for a mesh without a cutout, no automatic subdivision (Tessellation only), window moves/resizes inside the app (remembered), Anchor group (X, Y, Angle) and an angle knob on the orange growth line. It can't leave the TreeCraft window for another monitor (one OS window only).

- **Picture 11:** new points join the closest point; first anchor = Pivot (white, orange line); green anchors with their own angle lines; a Leaf generator under a Leaf generator spawns leaves on the parent leaves' green anchors (`gen.rs` ParentRef::Anchor, `meshio::anchor_points`). Unit tests: `cargo test`. Confirmed in the original (fns 0x1402456e0, 0x14024b880): children of a mesh with anchors go on its anchors, with an "Anchors" choice (All anchors, 1-5) and an "Unable to find anchor" warning; both are built. Not built: how First/Last filter anchors.

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering; the other slot pictures are stored only.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the original's Material Sets panel (members and weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). Ruled out: fns 0x140192780 and 0x140196510 (old-file converters) and fn 0x1403154a0 (image processing). Next: find code reading the Spine:Shape:Gravity property (index 130) from the branch node.
4. Estimated behaviour: what Tessellation and the Angle thumb wheel (turns the growth line) do to the mesh (their controls and the Load/Save arrows are confirmed from code), "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Missing: Cull backfaces and Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds", extra anchors; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.

- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab

- `props.rs`: Properties panel

- `model.rs`: data types and defaults

- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.

- If an open TreeCraft window locks `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, rename the file and rebuild; `treecraft-running-old.exe` there is such a leftover and can be removed once no copy is running.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. the mesh file loader fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.
- In PowerShell use absolute paths with `[IO.File]` calls (its working folder differs from PowerShell's).

# Handoff – TreeCraft (rebuild of a game tree modeler)

_Last updated 2026-11-10._

## Project
- Rust + macroquad desktop app in `app/`; program `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, window "TreeCraft".
- Original studied (Deep mode): `C:\Program Files\SpeedTree\SpeedTree Games Indie v8.4.2\win64\SpeedTree Modeler Games Indie.exe`.
- Values, rules and their function addresses: `MECHANICS.md` / `mechanics.json` (108 values: 91 sourced, 17 estimated). Original files used: `CREDITS.md`.

## Status
Builds with no errors and passes every Craft Anything check (build, screenshot, self-test, values sheet, credits). `cargo test` runs 3 unit tests (point insertion, anchor directions, LOD file search). The self-test doesn't open the Edit Cutout window.

## Done
- **Generation tab:** Tree/Trunk/Branch/Leaf node graph; Classic, Absolute and Interval placement from the original (Phyllotaxy approximate); Jink frequency (default 0.5). A Leaf generator can sit under a Leaf generator and spawns one leaf per green anchor of each parent leaf, with an "Anchors" choice (All anchors, 1-5) and the original's "Unable to find anchor" warning.
- **Properties panel (left):** shows the clicked node, material or mesh.
- **Viewport:** perspective/orthographic, orbit/pan/zoom/frame, grid, lighting.
- **Meshes tab** (pictures 1-3, 7): +/- Meshes window, empty new meshes, High/Med/Low files, "Embedded" label, Orient/Flip/winding processing from the original; wireframe preview with a Material switch and right-click Lit/Scribed.
- **Edit Cutout window** (pictures 9-11): embed warning; modal, movable/resizable (inside the app window), Confirm/Cancel only; starts with no points; new points join the closest point; outlines can't cross themselves (no masks); Reset Points/Anchors ask first; Pivot (white, orange angle line) and green anchors with their own angle lines; Options Tessellation (no automatic subdivision), Angle wheel, Double-sided, Improve folding (center point); High/Med/Low Load/Save arrows.
- **Materials tab** (pictures 4-6, 8): picker (hides sets), +/- window, + from texture files, copy/paste, Settings/Meshes sub-tabs, ten texture slots, original's defaults, Make New Set...; preview shapes Sphere/Plane/Cylinder/Custom, turns only when dragged, wheel zoom.
- **New tree:** starts with no materials, textures or meshes (the start-up demo tree has Bark, Leaf and Leaf cutout).

## Outstanding
1. Only the Color, Opacity and Normal slot pictures affect rendering.
2. Material sets draw as their first member; the Material Sets panel (members, weights) isn't built.
3. Branch bending (gravity, noise, jink) and radius taper are estimated (unknown unk_cb364103d504cff6). Ruled out: fns 0x140192780, 0x140196510 (old-file converters), 0x1403154a0 (image processing).
4. Estimated: what Tessellation and Angle do to the mesh, "Edit..." on an empty material mesh row. Not built: First/Last filtering of anchors, Cull backfaces / Show unique uvs in the mesh preview menu.
5. Stored but inactive: mesh Ripple, Proxy collision, Collection "Fronds"; material Season, Atlas, Max resolution, Unwrap, User data.
6. Not built: Displacements tab, Node/Freehand edit modes, six generation modes (Proportional, Proportional steps, Absolute steps, Bifurcation, Flood, Parent), property curves, save/load/export, wind. The Edit Cutout window can't move to another monitor (single OS window).

## Important files (`app/src/`)
- `app.rs`: app state, dock tabs, viewport, Meshes tab, node graph rules
- `cutout.rs`: Edit Cutout window (+ unit tests)
- `matpanel.rs`: Materials tab
- `meshdialog.rs`: shared add/remove window for meshes and materials
- `props.rs`: Properties panel
- `gen.rs`: tree growth, including anchor spawning
- `model.rs`: data types and defaults
- `render.rs`: shader, camera, preview shapes
- `textures.rs`: picture loading, adjustments, auto-cutout
- `meshio.rs`: OBJ files, cutout geometry, anchor points, mesh processing
- `ui.rs`: UI toolkit
- `main.rs`: menus, keys, `--screenshot`, `--self-test`

## Next tasks
1. Use the remaining slot pictures (Gloss, Specular, Metallic, Subsurface, AO) in the shader (`render.rs`).
2. Build the Material Sets panel (original fn 0x1400757b0).
3. Save/load trees, then export the whole tree (OBJ/FBX).
4. Property curves (Frequency, Length, Radius along the parent).
5. Find the original's branch-bending code: look for code reading the Spine:Shape:Gravity property (index 130) from the branch node; replace the estimates in `gen.rs`.
6. Read how First/Last filter anchors (parent mesh's placement call from fn 0x1402456e0) and add it.
7. Add Edit Cutout and anchor-spawning steps to the self-test.

## Useful tricks
- Screenshot start states: `TM_TAB=0..2`, `TM_SEL=<node name>|mat:N|mesh:N`, `TM_MATTAB=1`, `TM_DIALOG=1|mat|cut`, `TM_NEW=1`.
- UI scaling: `ui_scale()` / `ui_factor()` in `main.rs`.
- Real defaults live in the install's gzip XML files: `app_data\sketch\trunk.stt` / `branch.stt` and the `.spm` trees.
- Qt slot dispatchers: read the class's meta-object (stringdata lists slots in case order; extradata points at the dispatcher).
- If an open TreeCraft window locks `target/debug/treecraft.exe`, rename the file and rebuild; `treecraft-running-old.exe` there is such a leftover and can be removed once no copy is running.
- Ghidra fails on very large functions (e.g. fn 0x1400b19b0); use smaller callees.
- PowerShell: use absolute paths with `[IO.File]`; long replacement scripts can trip the safety check, so prefer the Edit tool.

The build has the Anchors choice on Leaf generators and shows that message in the status bar.
- The parent leaf mesh's placement (CLeafMeshNode vtable 0x141064e68, slot +0x4f8 = fn 0x14026f500) walks the mesh's anchors and keeps one when the restriction is 0 or equals the anchor's id, and when First <= v <= Last, where v is the anchor record's second number (read as its height along the leaf); the child's position is (v - First) / (Last - First) clamped to 0..1 (v itself when First = Last), and its Roll and other values are read there. The build filters anchors the same way using the anchor's height along the pivot's growth line in picture units (0 at the pivot, about 1 at the top of a full-height card). A Leaf generator added under a Leaf generator starts with First 0 and Last 1 so every anchor is used.

content.text:
I found where the original decides which anchors a child leaf generator uses, and added that rule to TreeCraft. An anchor is now used only if its height along the leaf falls between the generator's First and Last values, on top of last round's "Anchors" choice. A leaf generator you place under another leaf starts at 0 to 1, so it still uses every anchor until you change it. It builds and passes every check.

The original stores a number per anchor that it compares with First/Last, and I'm reading that number as the anchor's height along the leaf; that part is inferred, not confirmed. Your open TreeCraft window was locking the program file, so I left it running and set the old file aside under a new name before rebuilding.

Per level, the first arrow is LoadButton and the second SaveButton: load = edit that level in the window, save = put the window's shape into that level (as built). The canvas and the level column start at 600:100 in a splitter. The (unbuilt) mask colour defaults to red (QColor 7).

- At the person's request (picture-11): a new point is inserted next to the closest existing point (on the side that keeps the outline simple and adds the shorter edge). The first anchor is the Pivot (white, orange angle line: where the leaf attaches and grows). Other anchors are green, each with its own angle line (degrees clockwise from up in the picture). A Leaf generator placed under a Leaf generator spawns one leaf on each green anchor of each parent leaf, pointing along that anchor's line (its Start angle starts at 0; Roll turns it around the line; size, droop, twist etc. come from its own properties). The anchors go through the same Pivot angle, Orient, Flip, Scale, leaf size and fold as the mesh (curl is applied to position only). This follows the person's design, and the original confirms the shape of it: when a generator's parent is a mesh with anchors, the placement routine (fn 0x1402456e0) skips the generation modes and asks the parent mesh to place children on its anchors (filtered by the generator's First/Last and its "Generation:Anchors" choice); if none were placed it reports "Unable to find anchor for node (check mesh anchors (including LOD meshes), first/last, and anchor restrictions)". "Generation:Anchors" (fn 0x14024b880, next to Generation:Mode) offers All anchors, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The build has the Anchors choice on Leaf generators and shows that message in the status bar.

- The parent leaf mesh's placement (CLeafMeshNode vtable 0x141064e68, slot +0x4f8 = fn 0x14026f500) walks the mesh's anchors and keeps one when the restriction is 0 or equals the anchor's id, and when First <= v <= Last, where v is the anchor record's second number (read as its height along the leaf); the child's position is (v - First) / (Last - First) clamped to 0..1 (v itself when First = Last), and its Roll and other values are read there. The build filters anchors the same way using the anchor's height along the pivot's growth line in picture units (0 at the pivot, about 1 at the top of a full-height card). A Leaf generator added under a Leaf generator starts with First 0 and Last 1 so every anchor is used.

lines: - Controls (fns 0x1402f4120, 0x1402f83f0, class COptimalMeshDialog): Tessellation is a QSlider 0..10000, page step 100 (0..1 in the build); Angle is a CThumbWheel (fn 0x140409be0; the window sets its step to 2) sending AngleChanged; Double-sided and Improve folding are check boxes. Per level, the first arrow is LoadButton and the second SaveButton: load = edit that level in the window, save = put the window's shape into that level (as built). The canvas and the level column start at 600:100 in a splitter. The (unbuilt) mask colour defaults to red (QColor 7).

- At the person's request (picture-11): a new point is inserted next to the closest existing point (on the side that keeps the outline simple and adds the shorter edge). The first anchor is the Pivot (white, orange angle line: where the leaf attaches and grows). Other anchors are green, each with its own angle line (degrees clockwise from up in the picture). A Leaf generator placed under a Leaf generator spawns one leaf on each green anchor of each parent leaf, pointing along that anchor's line (its Start angle starts at 0; Roll turns it around the line; size, droop, twist etc. come from its own properties). The anchors go through the same Pivot angle, Orient, Flip, Scale, leaf size and fold as the mesh (curl is applied to position only). This follows the person's design, and the original confirms the shape of it: when a generator's parent is a mesh with anchors, the placement routine (fn 0x1402456e0) skips the generation modes and asks the parent mesh to place children on its anchors (filtered by the generator's First/Last and its "Generation:Anchors" choice); if none were placed it reports "Unable to find anchor for node (check mesh anchors (including LOD meshes), first/last, and anchor restrictions)". "Generation:Anchors" (fn 0x14024b880, next to Generation:Mode) offers All anchors, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The build has the Anchors choice on Leaf generators and shows that message in the status bar.

- The parent leaf mesh's placement (CLeafMeshNode vtable 0x141064e68, slot +0x4f8 = fn 0x14026f500) walks the mesh's anchors and keeps one when the restriction is 0 or equals the anchor's id, and when First <= v <= Last, where v is the anchor record's second number (read as its height along the leaf); the child's position is (v - First) / (Last - First) clamped to 0..1 (v itself when First = Last), and its Roll and other values are read there. The build filters anchors the same way using the anchor's height along the pivot's growth line in picture units (0 at the pivot, about 1 at the top of a full-height card). A Leaf generator added under a Leaf generator starts with First 0 and Last 1 so every anchor is used.

-- At the person's request (pictures 12-13): each level (High/Med/Low) keeps its own green anchors (position, angle, number) and point colours, as the original keeps anchors per level ("check mesh anchors (including LOD meshes)"); the -> arrow (SaveButton) copies the canvas's outline, colours and anchors into a level, <- (LoadButton) loads them, and each level preview draws its anchors in green with an "A:" count. The tree uses High's anchors (or the first level below that has some). Right-clicking a green anchor picks its number 1-5 (shown under it); the Anchors choice of generators matches that number (the original matches its anchor id, fn 0x14026f500). A Transform group moves, rotates or scales the whole card (points, pivot and anchors; rotation turns the angles too). The Color group (the original's place for it; swatch red by default, fn 0x1402f83f0) paints vertex colours on points with a brush; new vertices take the average of their source points; the colours multiply the leaf's colour on the tree.
